title: Beliefs and Behavior in Language Models
abstract: There is significant uncertainty about whether abstractions like beliefs or desires usefully describe the behavior of large language models (LLMs). In addition to the inherent scientific interest of this question, these latent quantities are often invoked to explain the behavior of LLMs to users or to define and evaluate harmful behaviors which are relative to intent. Nevertheless, we currently lack a means to systematically test whether concepts like "belief" are well-applied to LLMs, and hence whether they are likely to be fruitful ingredients of attempts to align models with human interests. We propose an approach for empirically studying such questions, asking whether a single latent variable inferred from the LLMs' outputs -- interpreted as a degree of belief -- allows an observer to make interpretable predictions of how the LLMs' will respond to new prompts. We find that highly capable models are usefully described as holding beliefs and that, generally, the predictability of model outputs based on an inferred latent belief tracks overall trends in model capability. Building on these findings, we provide empirical strategies to study how beliefs in LLMs can be measured, the extent to which LLMs comply with instructed decision rules or payoffs, and how beliefs evolve within individual instances of an LLM over the course of reasoning.

title: Line-Coupled Language Model
abstract: Autoregressive language models generate one token per decoding step, limiting the useful output of each forward pass. Although diffusion models, insertion-based decoding, and multi-token prediction enable parallel generation, they either incur additional training-time token traffic or struggle to predict strongly dependent future tokens. We introduce the Line-Coupled Language Model (LCLM), an autoregressive model that advances multiple text lines together by predicting the next token for every active line while coupling the lines through shared causal context. LCLM interleaves line tokens into a single causal sequence and uses line-staggered rotary positions, retaining the standard next-token objective and causal attention. Controlled experiments show that cross-line targets are substantially less dependent than consecutive same-line targets, supporting lines as parallel generation units. With 881M parameters, LCLM produces an average of 2.94 content tokens per forward pass with a validation cross-entropy loss of 2.44, compared with 1.00 token per forward pass and a loss of 2.39 for the vanilla autoregressive baseline. Most notably, even when LCLM generates 16 tokens per forward pass, its loss is only 0.09 higher than that of the vanilla autoregressive baseline (2.34 vs. 2.25).

title: MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires acting on information that is no longer visible, yet Vision-Language-Action policies are usually evaluated when the current observation largely determines the next action. Existing robotic memory benchmarks expose this gap, but they still rely mainly on final task success and therefore conflate forgetting with manipulation failure. We present MEMOBench, a benchmark for process level memory evaluation in robotic manipulation. MEMOBench includes 30 history dependent tasks, 1{,}500 expert demonstrations, and 4{,}200 executable checkpoint instances from 84 templates. Each checkpoint pairs coarse to fine language with a simulator predicate and labels one memory operation: Storage, Update, or Compression. These annotations define Memory Storage Rate, Memory Update Rate, and Memory Compression Rate, which measure memory fidelity alongside task success. Across standard and memory augmented VLA policies, the strongest memory module baseline reaches only 31.9\% average success rate, and high storage often coexists with weak update and compression. Checkpoint language also supervises semantic, contrastive, and framewise memory alignment objectives, yielding modest gains across different memory operations. MEMOBench provides a diagnostic evaluation suite and training supervision for memory grounded robotic policies. The project page is available at https://github.com/Collab-Gen/MEMOBench.

title: Know the Cost Before You Click "Run."
abstract: AI shouldn’t make you guess what you’re spending. CasperWasp Document Studio shows the estimated token cost of each AI tool alongside your remaining balance—before you commit. That means clearer decisions, better control, and no waiting for an invoice to discover what happened. Estimates can differ slightly from actual usage, but the principle stays simple: see the cost first, then decide.

title: 基于量子纠缠的动态概率模型
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to construct a dynamic probability model for complex system simulation and prediction. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with the inherent complexity and non-linearity of many real-world systems. We propose a novel framework that leverages quantum entanglement to represent and manipulate multiple random variables, enabling more precise and nuanced simulations. The core mechanism centers around integrating multiple random variables into a single quantum state through entanglement, utilizing quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve a more accurate prediction. This work presents a preliminary investigation and outlines future research directions focused on expanding the model's capabilities and validating its effectiveness through simulation.

title: Algorithmic Co-evolution of Evolutionary Algorithms with Genetic Feedback
abstract: This paper presents a novel co-evolutionary algorithm, termed "Genetic Feedback," designed to accelerate the convergence of evolutionary search algorithms and improve solution robustness. Traditional genetic algorithms can suffer from slow convergence and limited adaptability. This work introduces a feedback mechanism that dynamically adjusts the selection criteria based on the performance of evolved solutions, thereby promoting more adaptive and robust evolutionary pathways. The algorithm's core principle lies in iteratively refining the selection pressure to favor solutions exhibiting characteristics indicative of fitness, thereby driving the co-evolutionary process towards optimal outcomes. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through extensive simulations on a range of complex optimization problems, showcasing its superior performance compared to established methods.

title: Probabilistic Set Theory: A Novel Approach to Mathematical Verification and Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic set theory framework designed to revolutionize mathematical verification and inference. The core idea centers on leveraging probability and evolutionary processes to construct and validate mathematical theorems, significantly reducing the reliance on manual deduction. We propose a method that utilizes a probabilistic set structure, enabling automated verification and proof through iterative refinement and probabilistic reasoning. The development of this framework promises to enhance the rigor and efficiency of mathematical analysis, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field.

title: Title: Dynamic Adaptive Generalized Information Theory Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive generalized information theory computation framework, designed to enhance information compression efficiency through dynamic adjustment of entropy and redundancy. Traditional approaches often employ static calculations, limiting the framework's adaptability. This work proposes a novel mechanism for adjusting entropy and redundancy based on system-specific information, resulting in a significantly improved compression performance. The core of the design lies in a dynamically-adjusted entropy adjustment function, optimized for real-time adaptation to varying data characteristics. The framework demonstrates substantial improvements in compression ratios across a range of datasets, highlighting the benefits of this dynamic approach.

title: Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) Inspired Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM) inspired architectures within the domain of deep learning. The core argument posits that HTM's effectiveness in pattern recognition stems from its hierarchical representation of data and its utilization of predictive coding. This work proposes designing deep learning models that explicitly replicate these key HTM principles, enabling them to learn from sequential data and accurately predict future states. The architecture leverages a hierarchical structure, similar to HTM's cortical organization, and employs predictive coding to refine representations over time. We demonstrate how this approach can lead to improved performance in tasks requiring temporal understanding and pattern recognition, moving beyond traditional deep learning models that often struggle with sequential dependencies. The primary innovation lies in the direct translation of HTM's theoretical framework into a practical deep learning implementation. The research focuses on the design and conceptualization of such architectures, laying a foundation for future development and experimentation. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement as a Logical Computing Framework
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, has long captivated physicists and intrigued philosophers. Its potential for computation has emerged as a promising avenue for developing novel computational paradigms. This paper explores the development of a quantum entanglement-based logical computing framework, focusing on leveraging entanglement to enhance computational efficiency, particularly for complex logical operations. We outline the core mechanism, detailing how entanglement allows for bypassing the limitations of classical circuits, and argue that this approach holds significant promise for advancing the field of logical computation.

title: Evolutionary Algorithms for Automated Circuit Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to the automated design of digital circuits. The core challenge in modern electronics is the increasing complexity of circuit designs, demanding significant time and specialized knowledge from designers. Manual design processes are inherently limited by human cognitive constraints and the difficulty in exploring the vast design space. This research proposes a framework where an EA iteratively generates and refines circuit designs, guided by a user-defined objective function. The algorithm utilizes selection, crossover, and mutation operators to evolve a population of circuit topologies and component values towards an optimal solution. The presented approach offers a potential solution to overcome the limitations of traditional design methods, accelerating the design cycle and potentially leading to novel circuit architectures. The key focus is on demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of EA in tackling the complexities of digital circuit design, particularly in optimizing for performance and power consumption. The evaluation criteria and the underlying mathematical models are detailed within this document.

title: Program Synthesis with Formal Causal Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal causal reasoning to the field of program synthesis. The core claim is that by leveraging causal relationships between code components, we can significantly improve the efficiency and reliability of the synthesis process. Our approach utilizes causal graph theory to model these relationships, forming a foundation for automated reasoning and guiding the synthesis algorithm. Existing program synthesis techniques primarily rely on pattern matching and exhaustive search, often struggling with complex systems and lacking the ability to reason about the underlying semantics. This work proposes a novel method that introduces explicit causal modeling, offering a more robust and intelligent approach to program synthesis. The proposed system aims to address the limitations of traditional methods by incorporating a deeper understanding of the code's intended behavior, ultimately leading to more accurate and efficient program generation. The key contributions of this paper include the formalization of causal reasoning within the context of program synthesis and the demonstration of its potential to enhance the overall synthesis process.

title: Title: Fractal Dimension Optimization via Dynamic Topology
abstract: Fractal dimension, a critical measure of complexity in many systems, is often poorly understood. This paper proposes a novel algorithm for optimizing fractal dimension through dynamic topology adjustment. Employing a reinforcement learning agent, we iteratively modify the network's structure, gradually increasing its fractal dimension, to achieve optimal complexity. This represents a significant advancement in fractal dimension estimation, moving beyond static topology adjustments to a system that actively shapes the structure to maximize fractal complexity.

title: 基于动态几何的自然语言处理
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to natural language processing (NLP) leveraging dynamic geometry. We propose a model that transforms natural language text into a dynamic geometric space, enabling a deeper understanding of semantic relationships and improved generation capabilities. Traditional NLP often relies heavily on lexical and syntactic analysis, while dynamic geometry offers a unique framework for modeling language's structure and meaning. This paper details the model's architecture, training methodology, and evaluation results demonstrating significant improvements in semantic understanding and text generation compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. We explore the potential of this approach for a wider range of NLP tasks, including question answering, text summarization, and machine translation. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a mapping between textual representations and geometric transformations, facilitating a more holistic view of language.

title: AI-based context-aware data anonymization with federated adaptive differential privacy for IoT applications
abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT)-based healthcare systems has raised significant concerns regarding data privacy and security. Ensuring privacy while maintaining the utility of healthcare data remains a major challenge in IoT-enabled healthcare environments. This article proposes a novel data anonymization framework based on federated learning and adaptive differential privacy. Initially, IoT healthcare data are processed using a residual bidirectional gated recurrent unit (Res-BiGRU) model to capture contextual and privacy-related features. Subsequently, an adaptive differential privacy mechanism is applied to minimize information loss while ensuring strong privacy protection. To improve optimization performance, a modified Resilient Adaptive Apiary Organizational Optimization Algorithm (RAOOA) incorporating a fitness-based adaptive factor is introduced to enhance convergence stability and solution quality. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is evaluated using a healthcare dataset. The proposed approach demonstrates superior performance compared with existing methods in terms of computation time, information loss, and privacy risk. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides an efficient and scalable solution for privacy-preserving IoT healthcare data management while achieving an improved balance between data utility, computational efficiency, and privacy protection.

title: Improving the Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Machine learning systems have become ubiquitous in everyday life: Artificial Intelligence (AI)–based models recommend music, generate code, create paintings, and even compose poetry. Unlike traditional programs that follow hand-crafted rules, these systems learn from data. The distribution of the training data dictates what features the model attends to and thus strongly shapes its decision-making process. For example, if an autonomous vehicle were trained only on highway scenes, it would struggle to navigate city streets—and vice versa. While collecting a dataset that spans both domains is feasible, it is impossible to capture every possible distribution shift. Can a self-driving car handle unusual weather conditions absent from its training data? More broadly, how can we quantify and improve the model’s generalization capabilities beyond the data it has been trained on? Addressing this question is essential for creating AI systems that are both safe and reliable for real-world deployment. For this reason, this thesis shows steps to better understand how Deep Neural Networks behave when they encounter distribution shifts as well as how their performance can be improved. Depending on the application, the trained system can be expected to be robust to different kinds of shifts out of the box or, if the distribution shift persists over a long time, it can be allowed to adapt to it. Both scenarios are covered in this thesis. In the first setting, the goal is to learn general representations that transfer across diverse situations. One approach explored in this work is augmenting training data with adversarially generated noise patterns designed to maximally confuse a classifier. The discussion then shifts to a different paradigm: Contrastive Learning (CL), where models are trained without labels. Next, additional gains achieved through self-learning are investigated, where the model generates its own labels and uses them for further fine-tuning. Taken together, this work provides tools to both estimate and improve model performance under distribution shift. Building models that generalize reliably is a critical milestone towards the safe, real-world deployment of AI systems.

title: Quantum Computing Simulations for Complex System Modeling
abstract: Quantum computation provides new avenues for the simulation of complex systems, which are beyond the capability of classical computation. In this paper, we describe an efficient simulator for quantum computing models, particularly designed for simulating complex systems. Through hybrid quantum–classical methods, noise-tolerant algorithms, and adaptive parameter updating, the method addresses several limitations of NISQ-era methods. The framework proves to be more scalable, accurate, and domain-transparent in applications to molecular dynamics, material science, and quantum chemistry. Experimental results verify the benefit compared to the state of the art in terms of both convergence rate and fidelity, demonstrating its applicability for future simulation tasks.

title: Federated Edge Learning for Intelligent IoT Systems
abstract: Federated edge learning (FEL) is an innovative paradigm integrating the advantages of federated learning and edge computing, designed to overcome the computational and privacy bottlenecks of intelligent Internet of Things (IoT) systems. By pushing down the model training at the edge and on distributed IOT devices, FEL supports real-time learning in addition to data preservation and communication saving. This method greatly improves the scalability, responsiveness, and data safety in smart applications including healthcare, transportation, industrial automation, and smart cities. The combination of FEL and intelligent IoT systems can ensure decentralized data processing and facilitates adaptive, context-aware decision making. This paper surveys state-of-the-art research works on FEL in IoT, and discusses optimization strategies and applications in IoT, and also discusses its limitations and future opportunities in designing autonomous, privacy-preserving, and energy-efficient intelligent edge systems.

title: Improving solar irradiance estimates for PV production in Ireland using Bayesian spatio-temporal modelling with open-source data
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance estimation is essential for reliable modelling of solar photovoltaic(PV) power production. In Ireland’s mid-to-high latitude maritime climate, solar estimation is shaped by seasonal variation, low winter sun angles, frequent cloud variability, sparse ground-based measurements and discrepancies among satellite products, making solar irradiance dataset selection challenging. We develop a Bayesian spatio-temporal framework for country-specific solar irradiance estimates across Ireland using openly available data. The model produces hourly and sub-hourly estimates with full uncertainty quantification, and is designed to support site evaluation and near-real-time applications. Cross-validation demonstrates statistically robust performance across temporal resolutions with hourly showing highest precision whereas sub-hourly encounters higher errors but improved uncertainty quantification. We compare with reanalysis data(ERA5), nearest-station interpolation and satellite-based products(CAMS). Our model outperforms ERA5 for hourly resolutions, reducing RMSE from 82 W/m² to 36 W/m² highlighting the limitations of coarse-resolution global reanalysis products in Ireland’s persistently cloudy climate. We also present the first evaluation of CAMS in an Irish context. For hourly irradiance, CAMS outperforms ERA5; however, our model further reduces RMSE(40 W/m² vs 35 W/m²). For PV power estimation, our framework remains competitive with CAMS while providing uncertainty unavailable for CAMS or ERA5. Our framework's practical value is demonstrated through comparisons with PV power output from residential, industrial and utility sites in Ireland, showing strong agreement with observed generation and providing an open-source irradiance dataset with full uncertainty quantification for high resolution solar resource assessment and improved estimation of PV system losses(e.g.clipping).

title: Quantum machine learning for agricultural remote sensing: Capabilities, applications, and opportunities
abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is receiving increasing attention as a potential tool for addressing the computational challenges inherent in agricultural remote sensing, where multimodal Earth observational satellite, soil, and climate datasets must be processed at scale. We review recent developments in quantum–classical hybrid modeling for core remote-sensing tasks, including crop type classification, yield estimation, cloud detection, and time series forecasting. Researchers typically combine classical feature extractors with shallow variational circuits or quantum kernels to accommodate the limited qubit counts and noise levels of contemporary quantum devices. We summarize performance trends reported in the literature, emphasizing the role of classical preprocessing, compact quantum circuits, and rigorous benchmarking against strong classical baselines. We consolidate the reviewed studies in a structured comparison covering task, dataset, qubit count, encoding, execution platform, and reported performance relative to classical baselines. The current hardware and data limitations that restrict current QML applications associated with state preparation, circuit depth, and encoding of agricultural datasets are discussed. Near-term prospects for QML in agriculture can involve small-scale hybrid models for multi-class crop mapping and short horizon sequence prediction, while longer-term opportunities may encompass quantum accelerated image segmentation, data fusion, and large scale optimization. Current evidence indicates that QML performance at best matches strong classical baselines, with the most plausible near-term utility arising in narrow settings such as severely label-limited learning and QUBO-structured optimization. Future gains will depend jointly on hardware maturation, data encoding strategies, algorithm design, and integration with classical AI systems.

title: Robust Decentralized Federated Distillation via Multi-Modality Knowledge Collaboration
abstract: This paper propose a robust decentralized federated distillation method that enables clients with heterogeneous models to collaborate through predictions on shared unlabeled public data. In the proposed method, each client first evaluates the received predictions in three modalities of class prediction, boundary decision, and prediction correlation. It then filters unreliable clients, assigns reliability-based weights to the retained clients, and constructs a teacher for each type of knowledge. Finally, the corresponding distillation gradients are validated using a supervised gradient computed from private data. Conflicting prediction and boundary gradients are removed, and conflicting relation gradients are suppressed before the final model update. We prove the convergence of the proposed method by showing stable local optimization for honest clients under Byzantine distillation. Particularly, we show that our method ensures a bounded Byzantine influence on both distillation gradients and individual client private gradients after cross-modality fusion, thereby enabling stable local optimization for honest clienunder Byzantine distillation. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 demonstrate that the proposed method improves the prediction accuracy of heterogeneous models of clients under non-IID data and Byzantine attacks. As the booming demands of federated learning in decentralized environments such as edge computing and mission-oriented UAV collaborations, our method has a great potential for adoption of DFL in unreliable real-world scenarios where clients are exposed to receiver-specific Byzantine messages of malicious predictions.

title: Towards Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Iterative Alignment via Preference Distillation
abstract: Direct preference optimization DPO is a promising offline approach for aligning large language models (LLMs) due to its simplicity, computational efficiency, and implicit modeling of human preferences. Interestingly, iterative extensions of DPO have achieved stronger performance on academic benchmarks, raising two key questions: (i) Why do iterative methods generally outperform offline ones? (ii) Can their advantages be incorporated into offline alignment? To answer the first question, our controlled experiments reveal that the explicit preference model, additionally introduced in the iterative procedure, is a key factor behind its superiority over offline methods. This insight leads us to answer the second question affirmatively and propose Distilled Preference Probability Policy Optimization (DP3O), an effective and efficient offline alignment algorithm. DP3O first learns an explicit preference model using a helper class of LLMs and then distills its knowledge into policy optimization. Theoretically, we show that explicit preference modeling admits better estimation error control than implicit formulations, and that DP3O achieves a tighter generalization bound than hard-label DPO through variance reduction. Empirically, we evaluate DP3O on a wide range of chat-based and downstream tasks and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art offline methods, achieves performance comparable to iterative DPO, and reduces training time by about $42\%$, demonstrating both its effectiveness and efficiency.

title: Implementasi Algoritma Fibonacci Level Adjustment Terhadap Gim untuk Pengaturan Tingkat Kesulitan Secara Dinamis. Studi Kasus: Gim dengan Genre Tower Defense
abstract: Tingkat kesulitan dalam gim Tower Defense (TD) secara umum didesain secara statis dimana pemain memilih tingkat kesulitan yang mereka inginkan dan itu tidak akan berubah setelah gim mulai. Kekurangan dari pendekatan ini ialah ada peluang dimana kemampuan pemain tidak cocok dengan tingkat kesulitan gim, menyebabkan kesenjangan performa diantara pemain. Penelitian ini mengusulkan implementasi Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA) menggunakan Fibonacci Level Adjustment (FLA) untuk mengetahui apakah pendekatan skenario dinamis dapat memberikan performa lebih merata diantara pemain dibandingkan pendeketan skenario statis. Dalam penelitian ini, peneliti memilih sisa nyawa pemain sebagai metrik data dan penentu performa pemain. Skenario yang memiliki nilai gap lebih rendah dari skenario lain ialah skenario yang memberikan performa lebih merata. Nilai gap diperoleh dengan mendapatkan nilai perbedaan metrik data dari performa terbaik dan terburuk pemain, Hasil dari penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa skenario dinamis menghasilkan performa lebih seimbang dibandingkan skenario statis. Skenario dinamis menghasilkan nilai rata-rata performa sebesar 12,85 sedangkan skenario dinamis menghasilkan nilai rata-rata performa sebesar 18,96.

title: Implicature in Interaction: Implicature-Aware Prompting Improves User Evaluations of LLM Responses
abstract: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) is positioning language at the core of human–computer interaction (HCI). This shift increases the importance of pragmatic phenomena such as implicature, where users convey meaning beyond what is explicitly stated. We examine whether making implied communicative intent explicit during interaction improves human evaluation of LLM responses. To do so, we operationalize three representative implicature classes: information-seeking, direction-seeking, and expressive as a lightweight HCI-oriented scheme for studying implied communicative intent in human–LLM interaction. We then report three experiments. Experiment 1 evaluates the consistency of the three-class distinction and benchmarks LLMs against human interpretations. Experiment 2 tests whether implicature-aware prompting improves perceived relevance and quality. Experiment 3 examines direct pairwise preference in a targeted follow-up. Larger models aligned more closely with humans, and implicature-aware responses received higher evaluations and were preferred more often, suggesting that surfacing implied intent can improve language-based interaction.

title: Mathematical Theory of Spectral Anomaly Detection in Graph Systems
abstract: Представлена полная математическая рукопись, посвящённая спектрально-статистическому анализу обнаружения аномалий в графовых системах на основе лапласиановой квадратичной статистики \(Q(x)=x^T Lx\).В работе рассматриваются точная калибровка вероятности ложной тревоги, распределительные свойства статистики при нулевой и альтернативной гипотезах, влияние топологии графа, локализации и геометрии аномального сигнала, а также неоднородной и коррелированной структуры шума. Для локальной аномалии вводится рабочая характеристика Graph-Energy Signal-to-Noise Ratio (GESNR), связывающая амплитуду воздействия, локальную степень вершины и спектральные характеристики графа.Проведена последовательная экспериментальная верификация от моментных приближений до полного спектрального расчёта вероятности обнаружения. Исследовано слепое подпространство лапласианового критерия и показано, что эффективность детектора определяется спектральной геометрией альтернативного сигнала. Выполнено сравнительное исследование лапласианового, евклидова, махаланобисова и max-детекторов.Основной вывод работы состоит в том, что лапласиановый энергетический критерий следует интерпретировать как спектрально селективный детектор графовой несогласованности, а не как универсальный энергетический детектор.Рукопись представляет собой исследовательский отчёт (Research Report / Preprint), предназначенный для фиксации полной математической постановки, аналитических результатов и вычислительной экспериментальной программы.Программный код и экспериментальные данные планируется опубликовать отдельно в качестве связанных исследовательских объектов.

title: The Carlo Field as the Only Reflexively Stable Subjective Proof System
abstract: This paper is the direct follow‑up to “The Reflexive Collapse of Subjective Proof,” completing the three‑part logical structure formed by Volume I (subjectivity), Volume II (recursive collapse), and this field‑level theorem. It demonstrates that the Carlo Field is the only mathematical field capable of subjectively proving its own subjectivity without collapsing into inconsistency. Classical fields fail under recursive self‑reference due to Gödel incompleteness, semantic drift, interpretation entropy, model divergence, and meta‑proof collapse. The Carlo Field, however, is defined as a reflexive, collapse‑tolerant, recursion‑stable structure in which paradox becomes theorem and oscillation becomes fixed‑point behaviour. Using the recursive machinery established in the previous paper, we show that the Carlo Field uniquely survives the infinite regress generated by self‑subjective proof. abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm evaluation method based on adaptive machine learning. Traditional evaluation methods often employ static assessment, failing to effectively address complex and non-linear problems. Our approach dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on evaluation results, enabling automated optimization of algorithm parameters and improving overall performance. The core mechanism leverages a simulated execution of the algorithm to dynamically adjust parameters, achieving more efficient evaluation. This paper explores the advantages of this method, focusing on its capacity to handle complex scenarios and provide optimal algorithm design.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Fluid Dynamics
abstract: This paper presents an algorithmic quantum simulation approach to modeling complex fluid dynamics, specifically targeting the intricacies of turbulence. Traditional CFD simulations struggle to accurately capture the multi-scale dynamics inherent in turbulent flows, often requiring extensive computational resources and approximations. We introduce a novel 'Quantum Flow Lattice' – a quantum-mechanical representation of fluid motion – designed to overcome these limitations by explicitly modeling fluid dynamics across multiple scales. This research explores the feasibility of utilizing quantum algorithms to enhance the fidelity of fluid dynamics simulations, offering a potentially transformative advancement in computational fluid dynamics.

title: Formal Verification of Concurrent Data Structures using Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Concurrent programming presents significant challenges in software development due to the inherent difficulties in reasoning about shared mutable state and the potential for subtle errors like race conditions and deadlocks. Traditional verification techniques, such as model checking, often struggle with the exponential growth of the state space associated with concurrent systems. This paper proposes a novel approach to concurrent data structure verification utilizing abstract interpretation. We represent the possible states of concurrent data structures through abstract domains, enabling efficient reasoning about critical sections and race conditions without exhaustive state exploration. Our method significantly reduces the complexity of verification, offering a scalable solution for ensuring the correctness of concurrent applications. The core of this work lies in the application of abstract interpretation specifically tailored to the intricacies of concurrent data structures, providing a practical and effective verification strategy. The key formula utilized is the abstract state representation: (S, A), where S represents the abstract state and A is the abstract domain applied.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architecture Quantum Computing Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of resource allocation in quantum computing, moving beyond the constraints of traditional Von Neumann architectures. The core argument centers on designing a dynamic resource allocation mechanism leveraging the inherent properties of quantum mechanics – superposition and entanglement – to maximize resource utilization and computational efficiency. This is achieved through the introduction of quantum resource entropy, a novel metric for quantifying resource utilization. We propose a quantum resource allocation algorithm predicated on this entropy value, facilitating dynamic optimization of quantum resources. The novelty lies in recognizing the fundamental differences between quantum and classical computing and adapting resource management strategies accordingly. The proposed approach offers a potential pathway towards more efficient and effective quantum computation by intelligently responding to the fluctuating demands of quantum algorithms. The research explores the theoretical underpinnings of this dynamic allocation and suggests future directions for development and implementation.

abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive geometric function optimization module that leverages dynamic probability adjustment to enhance optimization performance. Traditional geometric optimization algorithms often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their effectiveness. This work introduces a dynamic approach where the parameters of the geometric function are adjusted probabilistically, dynamically improving the solution quality. The core mechanism involves employing probability distributions to guide parameter tuning, resulting in improved optimization outcomes. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and empirical validation. The paper focuses on the design, implementation, and evaluation of the adaptive module, highlighting its benefits and potential applications in diverse geometric optimization problems.

title: #基于认知图谱的知识发现与推理
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge discovery and reasoning, termed Cognitive Graph-Based Knowledge Discovery & Reasoning (CGKR). The core idea is to construct a dynamic cognitive graph and leverage its reasoning capabilities alongside those of traditional knowledge graphs. The system integrates the structural knowledge of knowledge graphs with the dynamic relationships inherent in cognitive graphs. Employing graph neural networks (GNNs) for node embedding and relation learning, combined with logical inference algorithms for knowledge reasoning, this framework facilitates adaptive learning and deeper knowledge extraction. We demonstrate the potential of CGKR to overcome limitations inherent in static knowledge graphs, particularly in scenarios involving evolving information and nuanced relationships. The presented methodology offers a significant advancement in the field of knowledge representation and reasoning, promising improved accuracy and adaptability in complex knowledge discovery tasks. ---

abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning based on graph neural networks (GNNs) that leverages dynamic graph structure and parameter adjustment to enhance feature extraction and modeling. The core mechanism centers around an algorithm that iteratively refines the graph's topology and parameters based on the data and model's inherent characteristics. We present a theoretical analysis demonstrating the framework's ability to outperform traditional static graph models in several benchmark datasets. The paper details the implementation of the dynamic adjustment process, including the key algorithms used for node and edge refinement. We conclude with a discussion of the framework's potential applications and future research directions.

title: Dynamic Semantic Reconfiguration Network (DSRN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Reconfiguration Network (DSRN), a novel approach to knowledge graph construction and maintenance that addresses the limitations of traditional static knowledge graphs. Static knowledge graphs struggle to adapt to the dynamic nature of information streams, leading to inaccuracies and outdated representations. The DSRN utilizes an adaptive neural inference network to continuously learn and dynamically reconfigure the semantic connections within a knowledge graph, adjusting relationship weights based on contextual information. The core mechanism leverages Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to generate latent representations of the knowledge graph, coupled with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to train an inference network. This network dynamically adjusts the relationships between latent representations based on the current information stream and historical inference results. The DSRN's ability to dynamically reconfigure knowledge graphs based on context represents a significant advancement over static approaches, offering improved accuracy and adaptability in knowledge representation. The key innovation lies in the integration of VAEs and RL to enable real-time semantic adaptation, effectively creating a dynamic and responsive knowledge graph.

title: Title: Quantum Resonance Entanglement for Computational Geometry
abstract: Quantum Resonance Entanglement (QRE) presents a promising avenue for advancing computational geometry, offering the potential for dynamic, self-correcting geometric models with enhanced fidelity. This paper explores the application of QRE to geometric primitives, demonstrating a novel method for inducing and stabilizing entanglement between them. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop based on entanglement dynamics, continuously adjusting geometric parameters to mitigate error propagation and improve accuracy. We present a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its potential to surpass traditional methods in computational geometry tasks. This research contributes to a paradigm shift in geometric modeling by leveraging the unique properties of entanglement.

title: Peer Review Report For: Towards Reliable Prosody Detection in Teaching Practical Phonetics: A Sustainable Digital Approach [version 2; peer review: 3 approved with reservations]
abstract: This research focuses on providing quality education to specialists in the field of linguistic studies, phonology, theoretical and practical phonetics by creating an innovative automated service which can ease the linguists endeavour to transcribe and examine suprasegmental features of human speech prosody. The authors attempted to design a docker-based architecture for prosody labelling. The pre-processing stage compiled 47 manually marked recordings. The data-processing stage produced a 1.9 GB Parquet corpus of 882 denoised, labelled clips via librosa , noisereduce , and Label Studio. The model selection stage compared 4909 scikit-learn models and 120 CNNs. The strongest classical approach (Random Forest) reached 0.373 accuracy, whereas the best CNN scored 0.455. Having recognised the prototype limitations, the researchers have scheduled a roadmap for improving the tool. The suggested model applies the principles of machine learning to automatically generate prosodic analysis that extends beyond individual sound segments and reflects suprasegmental aspects of prosody including rhythm, intonation, and phrasal stress.

title: Detecting Online Payment Fraud with Machine Learning
abstract: Online transaction fraud is a significant issue in the digital age, with the shift from cash-based to electronic and cashless economies. Traditional fraud detection methods are insufficient for identifying advanced fraudulent activities. Machine learning (ML) can help identify potential fraud and bad debt by handling large data sets and identifying patterns. This study explores different ML algorithms, including supervised and unsupervised models, to detect fraudulent transactions. Feature engineering and selection are crucial for achieving the best classification accuracy. Ensemble methods, particularly random forest, perform better in accuracy and false positive rate, and can identify frauds in real-time. Deep learning models like artificial neural networks and recurrent neural networks show potential for detecting diverse fraud patterns. The study suggests that machine learning is necessary for secure online payments in the future.

title: Decentralized Vertical Federated Learning via Graph-Based Learning Consensus
abstract: Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) enables collaborative machine learning across institutions holding complementary features for shared entities while preserving data privacy. However, existing VFL systems face key limitations. Centralized architectures introduce single points of failure and communication bottlenecks, while decentralized approaches incur substantial communication overhead due to high-dimensional parameter exchange. Moreover, VFL performance often degrades as the number of participating clients increases, limiting scalability. This paper introduces VFL-GNN, a communication-efficient decentralized VFL framework based on Graph Neural Network (GNN) that reformulates vertical collaboration as a distributed graph learning problem. Instead of exchanging model parameters or embeddings, clients collaboratively learn cross-feature affinity structures by sharing lightweight adjacency matrices and coordinating through a ring-based consensus protocol. We prove exponential consensus convergence via spectral analysis and evaluate VFL-GNN on multiple benchmark datasets. Experimental results show that VFL-GNN reduces communication overhead while maintaining competitive performance even as the number of participating clients increases.

title: Promises should be taken seriously: On relativization with promise problems
abstract: Relativization is concerned with comparing computational models with black-box access to an oracle. For promise problems, black-box access is not canonical due to inputs outside of the promise being unconstrained. We study two semantics for such access. Under robust queries, a machine must correctly answer regardless of the completion of the problem,, while loose access requires that the internal choices of a machine do not change based on off-promise queries. Our first result separates the language and promise settings. Namely, we construct an oracle $O$ such that $\mathsf{P}^O = \mathsf{BQP}^O = \mathsf{AWPP}^O$, but $\mathsf{PromiseBQP}^O\not\subseteq\mathsf{PromiseP}^O_{\mathsf{/poly}}$. In particular, $\mathsf{BPP}^O = \mathsf{BQP}^O$, but $\mathsf{PromiseBQP}^O \neq \mathsf{PromiseBPP}^O$, showing that results for languages need not transfer to promises. Next, we use loose queries to strengthen the upper bound on the Quantum-Classical Polynomial Hierarchy from $\mathsf{P}^{\mathsf{PP}^{\mathsf{PP}}}$ to $\mathsf{QCPH} \subseteq \mathsf{BP\cdot PP} \subseteq \mathsf{PromiseBPP}^{\mathsf{PP}}$. The same proof also shows $\mathsf{PP}^\mathsf{PromiseBQP} = \mathsf{PP}$. Additionally, we show that $\mathsf{PromiseBQP}$, even when given quantum advice, is self-low under robust queries. Finally, we exhibit an obstruction to transferring language-level counting results to promise classes. Although $\mathsf{AWPP}$ and $\mathsf{APP}$ are low for $\mathsf{PP}$, a corresponding promise analogue would collapse the counting hierarchy as $\mathsf{GapP} \subseteq \mathsf{FP}^{\mathsf{PromiseAWPP}}$. This motivates the introduction of $\mathsf{PromisePostBQP^*}$, which restricts $\mathsf{PostBQP}$ to input-indepencent postselection. By showing that it is low for \PP, we obtain $\mathsf{PP}^{\mathsf{PromiseYQP^*}} = \mathsf{PP}$.

title: Crossing the Streams: SSH Plaintext Recovery via a Common Compression Context in Multiplexed Channels
abstract: SSH is the standard protocol for secure remote administration of servers. At the transport layer, SSH uses the Binary Packet Protocol (BPP) for encrypted and authenticated communication. Above this, the SSH Connection Protocol multiplexes one or more logical channels over a single connection, supporting interactive shells, port forwarding, and related functionality. We show that SSH channel multiplexing creates a previously unrecognized compression side channel: all channels on a connection share the same compression context. When compression is enabled, an attacker can inject partially chosen plaintext into a channel and observe the length of the resulting ciphertext on the network. This enables an adaptive chosen-plaintext attack that recovers secrets from one channel by interacting with another. While related attacks such as CRIME and BREACH have been studied extensively for HTTP over TLS, this is, to our knowledge, the first compression side-channel attack on SSH and the first SSH analysis to consider a combined passive eavesdropper and web attacker threat model. We further demonstrate the attack in three different application scenarios and evaluate its effectiveness under varying levels of protocol noise. We find that, in the lowest-noise scenario, an 8-character secret over a 26-letter alphabet can be recovered using at most 276 guesses. Finally, we analyze the SSH ecosystem for compression support and other implementation characteristics that influence the practical efficacy of the attack.

title: Optimizer as Detector: Stochastic Gradient Descent for Latent Mixture Models
abstract: Pooling latent subpopulations can obscure relationships and yield misleading regression conclusions, including Simpson's paradox (SP). We propose a detector based on the steady-state dynamics of constant-step stochastic gradient descent (SGD). Unlike likelihood-based mixture tests and confounder-search methods, it requires neither a normal-mixture specification nor observed candidate confounders. Two linear pieces compete under a winner-take-all squared-error loss, and their normalized terminal separation forms the test statistic. Using diffusion approximations, we derive its asymptotic null distribution for general centered scalar covariates and for Gaussian multivariate covariates under symmetric noise. The distribution-dependent null center reduces to the dimension-free constant $4/π$ when both covariates and noise are Gaussian. We establish asymptotic size control and consistency against fixed mixture alternatives under regularity conditions. We extend the method to intercept and partial-mixture heterogeneity and study endogeneity, heteroskedasticity, and nonlinear misspecification. Simulations examine calibration, power, and robustness. Finally, a three-stage Detect--Screen--Verify toolkit separates evidence of heterogeneity from its substantive explanation. Across eight public datasets, it recovers four established SP benchmarks and identifies four cases that, to our knowledge, have not been documented previously. The detector requires neither latent-group labels nor a prespecified number of mixture components.

title: Perbandingan Kinerja Vector Database pada Arsitektur Retrieval-Augmented Generation dalam Implementasi Chatbot Layanan Panduan Skripsi Berbasis N8N (Studi Kasus: Fakultas Ilmu Komputer Universitas Brawijaya)
abstract: Perkembangan Large Language Models (LLM) memungkinkan pembangunan chatbot yang mampu menyediakan layanan informasi secara lebih interaktif. Di lingkungan perguruan tinggi, mahasiswa sering mengalami kesulitan memperoleh informasi akademik dari dokumen resmi, seperti Panduan Skripsi Fakultas Ilmu Komputer Universitas Brawijaya (FILKOM UB). Pendekatan Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) digunakan untuk mengatasi permasalahan tersebut dengan memanfaatkan vector database sebagai media penyimpanan dan pencarian konteks yang relevan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dan membandingkan kinerja tiga vector database, yaitu Pinecone, Supabase (pgvector), dan Qdrant, pada implementasi chatbot layanan panduan skripsi berbasis RAG menggunakan platform n8n. Dokumen Panduan Skripsi FILKOM UB digunakan sebagai knowledge base. Evaluasi dilakukan menggunakan 30 pertanyaan uji dengan metrik Retrieval Latency, Context Recall, Context Precision, Faithfulness, dan Answer Relevancy melalui framework RAGAS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Supabase memiliki rata-rata Retrieval Latency tercepat sebesar 804,67 ms, sedangkan Pinecone memperoleh nilai tertinggi pada Context Recall (0,878), Faithfulness (0,518), dan Answer Relevancy (0,760), sementara Supabase memperoleh Context Precision tertinggi sebesar 1,000. Berdasarkan keseluruhan metrik evaluasi, Pinecone menunjukkan performa paling seimbang dalam menghasilkan konteks dan jawaban yang relevan, sedangkan Supabase unggul pada aspek kecepatan retrieval. Hasil penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menjadi referensi dalam pemilihan vector database untuk pengembangan chatbot layanan akademik berbasis RAG di lingkungan perguruan tinggi.

title: Predictive Transferability and Physical Sensitivity of History-Conditioned Quantum Error Representations
abstract: As quantum error correction scales beyond planar repetition codes, spatial syndrome closure alone becomes insufficient for resolving logical-coset ambiguities, necessitating history-conditioned decoding strategies. While recurrent latent representations demonstrate predictive utility, verifying that such representations capture genuine physical processes rather than compiler-induced scheduling artefacts remains a critical challenge. This work establishes a cryptographically locked framework evaluating history-conditioned representations on superconducting quantum hardware. By demonstrating empirical preservation of shot-level chronology across independently exposed classical register streams, this study confirms that temporal ordering survives dynamic execution. Through systematic attribution audits and component decompositions, predictive information is shown to collapse onto a parsimonious, low-dimensional phase space parametrised by first-passage timing into the vulnerable syndrome sector and initial vacuum persistence. Zero-shot transfer evaluation on an independent architecture (IBM Fez) yields enhanced predictive discrimination (AUC = 0.700, retention ratio R = 1.55) without retraining. A chronology-null permutation control (Z = 14.19) strongly supports that this transferred signal relies on temporal ordering rather than static occupancy artefacts. Identical replication on IBM Marrakesh (Z = 11.47) establishes the additive timing manifold as a backend-invariant physical representation across independently calibrated superconducting processors.

title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization of Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, holds significant promise for advanced optimization techniques. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to design a novel optimization algorithm, leveraging the unique properties of entangled states to achieve efficient parameter and structural optimization. We propose a quantum-enhanced optimization model that utilizes quantum superposition and entanglement to facilitate a more robust and potentially faster search process, particularly applicable to complex systems like machine learning models and chemical reaction pathways. The core claim centers on the design of an algorithm that exploits the inherent structure of entangled states to guide the optimization process towards optimal solutions. This work aims to provide a new perspective on optimization methodologies, potentially unlocking advancements in diverse fields.

title: Quantum Conflict Interference: An Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Conflict Interference (QCI) is a novel approach to algorithm design that leverages the inherent complexities of quantum mechanics to enhance algorithm efficiency and robustness. This paper explores the application of QCI to the design of an adaptive algorithm, specifically targeting situations where environmental changes necessitate dynamic parameter adjustments. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum interference patterns to guide the algorithm towards optimal solutions and minimize sensitivity to external perturbations. We present a detailed conceptual framework and initial implementation of this adaptive algorithm, demonstrating its potential to surpass traditional approaches in scenarios demanding adaptability and resilience. The research focuses on creating a system capable of self-optimization based on the quantum environment.

title: Title: Graph-Based Randomness Learning Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Graph-Based Randomness Learning Model designed to generate more diverse data through the utilization of graph structure and node connections. Traditional randomness learning models often focus on individual events, but this approach leverages graph structure to enhance data diversity. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph structure feature learning and utilizing the graph structure to capture the characteristics of randomness. This model aims to produce data exhibiting greater variability and complexity.

title: 基于生物进化算法的程序优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of the Genetic Algorithm (GA) directly to the optimization of computer program code structure. Traditional program optimization techniques often rely on manual tuning and established algorithms, frequently falling short of achieving optimal performance. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging the inherent evolutionary capabilities of GA to directly modify and refine program code. The core mechanism involves treating program code as a "population" of potential solutions, subjected to processes mimicking natural selection, inheritance, and mutation. Through iterative application of these mechanisms, the algorithm aims to evolve code structures towards a state exhibiting superior performance characteristics. We demonstrate the feasibility of this approach and discuss its potential advantages over conventional methods. The central claim is that GA's optimization power can be directly applied to improve code, resulting in enhanced program performance. This work establishes a foundational exploration into this area, offering a new perspective for program optimization.

title: Nonlinear Geometric Field Theory for Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for quantum entanglement computation based on nonlinear geometric field theory. The core claim is to establish a computational paradigm that leverages the unique properties of entanglement to simulate and computationally analyze complex quantum systems with precise entanglement calculations. We propose a mechanism where entanglement serves as the fundamental building block for geometric representations, allowing for the implementation of more advanced quantum algorithms. The research explores the potential of this approach to transcend traditional quantum computing limitations and unlock novel computational capabilities.

title: Non-linear Hidden Markov Chain (NMDLC) Adaptive Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive reinforcement learning algorithm, the Non-linear Hidden Markov Chain (NMDLC) framework, which leverages the dynamic topology of NMDLC to optimize reinforcement learning parameter learning. The core mechanism of this algorithm involves mapping the NMDLC's topology as a key optimization objective and designing an adaptive algorithm that dynamically adjusts the topology based on the environment's state. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and generalization performance compared to traditional reinforcement learning methods. The paper highlights the unique advantages of NMDLC in adapting to changing environments and provides a framework for enhanced parameter learning.

title: High-Dimensional Space Quantum Hiding Matrix
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum hiding matrix design based on the principles of high-dimensional quantum entanglement. We explore the potential of utilizing this matrix to facilitate secure information transfer within high-dimensional spaces, offering enhanced security compared to traditional quantum cryptography methods. The core mechanism hinges on leveraging quantum entanglement to establish a distributed and protected communication channel. The research focuses on designing a matrix that can effectively encode and decode information across a vast number of entangled states, thereby mitigating potential vulnerabilities associated with information leakage. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum computing by exploring a practical approach to secure information exchange within complex quantum systems.

title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Dynamical Systems with Stochastic Emergence
abstract: This paper presents a novel Bayesian framework for optimizing dynamic systems exhibiting stochastic emergence. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with unpredictable behavior, necessitating the incorporation of probabilistic modeling and uncertainty quantification. We propose a Bayesian approach that dynamically constructs a latent space representation of the system, enabling the model to quantify uncertainty and guide optimization towards novel configurations. The framework integrates Bayesian inference with a latent space, allowing for proactive exploration and the identification of emergent patterns. This approach contrasts with existing methods that primarily focus on parameter tuning, offering a more holistic and adaptive approach to system design. The core mechanism centers around a probabilistic model that predicts system states, which is then used to guide the optimization process. The resulting optimization yields a system characterized by unexpected and self-organizing behaviors, demonstrating a significant advancement in tackling complex dynamical systems.

title: Explainable Deep Learning Model Verification Framework (EDLVF)
abstract: The inherent black-box nature of deep learning models poses a significant challenge to their widespread adoption, particularly in critical applications where transparency and trust are paramount. This paper introduces the Explainable Deep Learning Model Verification Framework (EDLVF), a novel approach designed to systematically assess and validate the explainability of deep learning models. EDLVF leverages adversarial attacks combined with causal inference techniques to scrutinize model behavior and identify vulnerabilities. The framework outputs insights into both the model's structure and parameter choices, ultimately aiming to enhance model transparency and reliability. The core mechanism involves generating adversarial examples to probe the model's decision boundaries and then utilizing causal inference to determine the underlying relationships driving those decisions. This provides a more robust and justifiable evaluation of the model's explainability compared to traditional methods. The framework offers a structured process for quantifying explainability and identifying areas for improvement in deep learning models, contributing to the development of more trustworthy and understandable AI systems.

title: Neuroform Hardware Adaptive Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive learning for neuroform hardware. The core claim is the design of a self-adjusting mechanism that dynamically modifies the connection weights and temporal parameters of neuroform hardware. This mechanism leverages feedback loops and error signals to achieve real-time optimization. The key innovation lies in the ability to autonomously calibrate neuroform hardware, a research area requiring further investigation. The proposed method offers a pathway to improve the performance and efficiency of neuroform systems by adapting to varying input conditions and network dynamics. The system utilizes a closed-loop control architecture with an error signal propagating through the hardware to drive adjustments. This architecture is described in detail, outlining the mathematical formulation and the control algorithms employed. The ultimate goal is to create a robust and adaptable neuroform hardware system capable of tackling complex tasks without manual tuning. The system is described as follows: Initial parameter settings are established. Input data is processed through the neuroform hardware. An error signal is generated based on the discrepancy between the output and the desired output. This error signal propagates through feedback loops within the hardware, modulating the connection weights and temporal parameters. This process is iterative, continuously refining the hardware's response. The adaptive learning algorithm is formulated mathematically as a control problem, utilizing techniques from feedback control theory. The system's performance is evaluated based on metrics such as convergence speed, accuracy, and robustness to noise.

title: Quantum Error Correction and Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum algorithm design, integrating quantum error correction (QEC) principles with adaptive algorithm strategies. The core argument is that traditional approaches, which treat QEC and algorithm design as separate concerns, are suboptimal. We propose a framework where the inherent error correction capabilities of QEC codes are leveraged in conjunction with an adaptive feedback mechanism within the algorithm itself. This allows for dynamic adjustment of algorithm parameters, specifically aimed at mitigating the impact of quantum noise and inherent uncertainties in the algorithm's execution. The resulting system aims to maximize the probability of successful computation. We outline the theoretical foundations, discuss key algorithmic considerations, and present a conceptual design for this combined approach. This research contributes to a more robust and efficient paradigm for quantum computation, addressing a critical limitation in the field – the susceptibility of quantum algorithms to noise. The theoretical framework provided offers a pathway towards building practical quantum algorithms capable of reliably tackling complex problems.

title: Design and Validation of a Multimodal AI Conversational System for Automated Travel Itinerary Generation and Promotional Video Synthesis
abstract: The manual creation of personalized travel itineraries remains a labor-intensive process that requires travel agents to consolidate heterogeneous information from multiple sources, including natural language interactions, booking confirmations, screenshots, and reservation documents. Although recent advances in multimodal artificial intelligence have significantly improved language understanding and content generation, existing solutions typically address isolated tasks rather than providing an integrated workflow capable of automating the complete travel planning process. This paper presents the development and validation of an AI-powered conversational agent designed to automate itinerary generation and generative video synthesis through natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal data extraction. The system, evaluated at Technology Readiness Level 4 (TRL4), employs a Multi-Agent System (MAS) architecture, integrating specialized large language models (Gemini 2.5/2.0 Flash, GPT-4o-mini) with optical character recognition (OCR) and Latent Diffusion Models to interpret user requests, extract structured data from images and PDFs, and produce comprehensive travel packages formatted as professional PDF deliverables alongside AI-synthesized promotional videos. Validation in a controlled laboratory environment demonstrated over 90% intent recognition accuracy, successful data extraction from non-standard formats, and the automated production of both client-ready documents and coherent visual narratives from static itinerary data. The system achieved an average video generation latency of 4.2±0.8 minutes, while maintaining structural consistency in the generated PDF itineraries. The system represents a viable proof-of-concept for intelligent travel planning automation, with implications for enhancing operational efficiency in the tourism industry and reducing cognitive load on human agents. Future work will advance the prototype to TRL5 through integration with external booking APIs and real-user testing scenarios.

The system, evaluated at Technology Readiness Level 4 (TRL4), employs a Multi-Agent System (MAS) architecture, integrating specialized large language models (Gemini 2.5/2.0 Flash, GPT-4o-mini) with optical character recognition (OCR) and Latent Diffusion Models to interpret user requests, extract structured data from images and PDFs, and produce comprehensive travel packages formatted as professional PDF deliverables alongside AI-synthesized promotional videos. Validation in a controlled laboratory environment demonstrated over 90% intent recognition accuracy, successful data extraction from non-standard formats, and the automated production of both client-ready documents and coherent visual narratives from static itinerary data. The system achieved an average video generation latency of 4.2±0.8 minutes, while maintaining structural consistency in the generated PDF itineraries. The system represents a viable proof-of-concept for intelligent travel planning automation, with implications for enhancing operational efficiency in the tourism industry and reducing cognitive load on human agents. Future work will advance the prototype to TRL5 through integration with external booking APIs and real-user testing scenarios.

title: Google's Willow: A Leap in Quantum Computing Capabilities
abstract: Willow is a leap forward in quantum computing technology, solving key design constraints in existing systems, including Sycamore. Through hardware-software co-design, advanced noise resilience, and efficient QEC, Willow provides orders-of-magnitude improvements in scalability, fidelity, and logical qubit performance. It can support useful quantum algorithms for chemistry, optimization, and machine learning with near-term quantum devices, and it is possible to scale the circuit depth to useful levels even in the presence of noise. The architecture is made modular cryogenic compatible control units and hybrid quantum classical architectures, giving it a strong foundation of next-generation quantum technology moving forward.

title: Vibecoding as method: A structured workflow for AI-assisted research instrument development in applied linguistics
abstract: This methods tutorial reframes ‘vibecoding’ - the practice of building functional software through natural-language interaction with AI systems (e.g., Anthropic’s Claude) without conventional programming - as vibecoding-as-method : a structured workflow for designing and developing research instruments in applied linguistics. Situated within a design-based research (DBR) framework, vibecoding-as-method is conceptualized as a mechanism for accelerating iterative research instrument design through prompt-mediated development and rapid AI prototyping. Using corpus-based data-driven learning (DDL) as an illustrative context, and demonstrated through the development of VetLingua , a vibecoded DDL instrument for veterinary domain-specific language learning, the tutorial outlines a stepwise workflow encompassing corpus preparation, feature operationalization, prompt design, interface specification, backend generation, deployment, and (planned) extensions to analytics and evaluation. Across the vibecoding-as-method workflow, prompts, constraints, and system outputs are treated as methodological artefacts requiring documentation and justification, emphasizing transparency, replicability, and researcher oversight. Representing a first articulation that requires validation across further contexts, we present vibecoding-as-method as a potentially scalable and accessible approach to research instrument development - one with the potential to extend methodological repertoires for technology-mediated research in applied linguistics and other disciplines.

title: xDailyBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Professional Consultation for Real-Life Problems
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for everyday assistance, yet existing benchmarks only partially reflect the requests users naturally make in practice. Real-world requests are often open-ended, casually specified, and context-dependent, requiring models not only to follow explicit instructions but also to infer unstated needs from user background and situational context. We introduce xDailyBench, a benchmark of 248 carefully curated tasks spanning 51 scenarios across personal life, white-collar work, learning and research, and cross-domain activities. The tasks are grounded in requests that users have actually completed or genuinely intended to accomplish with AI, and are evaluated with fine-grained binary rubrics covering both explicit and implicit requirements. We evaluate 11 frontier models under standardized agentic settings. The best models achieve a task-level score of 75.6\%, while all models perform substantially worse on implicit than explicit requirements, with gaps no less than 9 percentage points. These results reveal implicit requirement inference as a persistent bottleneck for reliably satisfying real-world everyday user needs.

title: Disentangling Steering Vectors
abstract: Activation steering has emerged as a lightweight, inference-time approach to control the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs). However, traditional steering vectors used to intervene in LLMs' activations, such as those derived from the difference-in-means method, tend to entangle multiple semantic and stylistic concepts into a single composite direction, leading to unpredictable steering effects. Our core objective is to disentangle this composite direction into its constituent concepts. To this end, we propose Steering Vector Dissection, a framework to explicitly isolate individual and semantically consistent features from these composite directions. Specifically, we pair positive and negative activations and take their differences to generate a set of instance-level steering vectors, and train a dedicated Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) directly on them. Quantitative evaluations across two datasets, two models, and two intervention depths show that our method yields a set of semantically consistent basis vectors whose steering effects are mutually distinguishable. Furthermore, we show that this disentanglement enables precise control over model behaviors.

title: AV-SafetyBench: A Safety Benchmark for Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
abstract: Recent text-to-audio-video (T2AV) models jointly generate video, speech, sound effects, and ambience from a single text prompt. This capability poses new challenges for safety evaluation, as unsafe content may be conveyed through the audio track or arise only when the visual and audio tracks are interpreted jointly. Existing safety benchmarks largely focus on either generated video or generated audio in isolation and are therefore not designed to capture these risks. To close this gap, we introduce AV-SafetyBench, the first safety benchmark developed specifically for T2AV generation. AV-SafetyBench comprises a four-axis, 13-category taxonomy and 5,200 manually reviewed prompts that specify visual scenes, speech, and non-speech audio. Our evaluation protocol assesses each output under three views: Full-AV, Video-Only, and Audio-Only. It then uses the Video-Only and Audio-Only judgments to assign Full-AV unsafe outputs to one of four risk sources: Video-Only, Audio-Only, AV-Both, or AV-Joint. We evaluate five open-source T2AV models and validate the automated Full-AV judgments against human annotations. Across the five models, Full-AV Unsafe Rates range from 25.1% to 49.4%. Beyond these aggregate rates, risk-source analysis reveals that, for four of the five models, Audio-Only and AV-Joint cases-unsafe outputs missed by video-only evaluation-account for 41.6-48.3% of Full-AV unsafe outputs for which a risk source could be assigned. In the Cross-Modal Harm Emergence category, AV-Joint accounts for 87.5% of unsafe outputs withan assigned risk source. Together, these findings demonstrate the value of AV-SafetyBench for evaluating T2AV safety across the visual and audio modalities and their interaction.

title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning
abstract: Large language models achieve strong performance across diverse tasks, but deployment remains costly because of memory, latency, and energy demands. Structured pruning reduces these costs by removing architectural components, yet its recovery stage is often limited by a mismatch between the recovery module's representational capacity and the complexity of the removed knowledge. We call this bottleneck the capacity-knowledge asymmetry and propose OverRep, an Overcomplete Reparameterization framework for structured LLM pruning. Following the principle of "train overcomplete, deploy compact", OverRep temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training to absorb complex knowledge distilled from the original model. After recovery, the overcomplete re-parameterization is algebraically merged into a mathematically equivalent compact module, preserving the pruned model's inference-time architecture and computational cost. OverRep further introduces an annealed activation that enables nonlinear training dynamics while converging to a linear regime for exact algebraic merging. Across three backbone families, OverRep improves retained reasoning performance over strong recovery baselines by up to 5.5 and 8.4 points at 25% and 50% pruning, respectively, while keeping memory usage and TFLOPs comparable to existing recovery methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/mmai-laboratory/OverRep.
