title: Zero-Shot Evaluation of Multilingual Models for Bidirectional English–Indic Machine Translation
abstract: The recent outbreak of Large Language Models~(LLMs) has radically changed the state of machine translation~(MT), which has provided fresh possibilities to low-resource and morphologically rich language pairs. The paper is a detailed comparative analysis of five state-of-the-art models, BLOOMZ, IndicTrans2, Krutrim, Sarvam~AI, and Aya-101, in a zero-shot translation paradigm between English and four typologically different languages, Indic languages: Gujarati, Malayalam, Hindi, and Tamil. The analysis compares general-purpose multilingual LLMs to specialised neural machine translation systems (NMT) in a systematic way balancing the generality of multilingual coverage and task specialisation. Every model is tested on the FLORES-200 DevTest corpus against three complementary testing metrics, BLEU, chrF++ and COMET. The languages selected represent two different linguistic families, that is, Indo-Aryan (Hindi, Gujarati) and Dravidian (Tamil, Malayalam), which gives them a principled ground of cross-family comparison. Experimentation findings indicate that there is significant performance difference among language pairs, translation directions and models. Specialised Indic models are proven to have marked morphologically rich languages of Dravidian language families on both semantic and character-level measures, LLM instruction-tuned models are also shown to achieve good performance in limited resources environments with respect to BLEU. The results of our work provide practical recommendations in the selection of LLM in the production Indic MT pipeline and emphasize the importance of the linguistic family factor in the assessment of the multilingual model.

title: Revisiting noise in learning: A generalized fractional Tikhonov approach within the adaptive network-based fuzzy inference system for classification problems
abstract: In machine learning, noise has traditionally been regarded as a detrimental factor. However, recent studies have revealed its potential to enhance learning through mechanisms such as noise-induced regularization and data augmentation. Building upon the established connection between input noise injection and Tikhonov regularization, this study proposes a generalized fractional Tikhonov regularization within the Adaptive Network-Based Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) framework. We introduce a novel model, ANFIS-GT, generalizing the previous ANFIS-T scheme, which has been the first ANFIS variant equipped with fractional Tikhonov regularization, in order to improve its classification performance. The proposed method employs differential quadrature rules to construct the regularization matrix in the penalty term, extending the conventional fractional Tikhonov approach that assumes an identity matrix. We formally prove the error stability of the new scheme, establishing a result that also holds for the former ANFIS-T under certain conditions, for which stability had not previously been demonstrated. Furthermore, we analytically identify the conditions under which the solution of the proposed scheme is equivalent to that obtained by small perturbations of the system’s input in a non-penalized error function. Extensive evaluations on binary and multiclass classification tasks demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, validating the theoretical developments and yielding a robust, interpretable, and effective learning model.

title: Disentangling decoder capacity and directionality in type constrained knowledge graph link prediction
abstract: Decoder comparisons in typed knowledge graph (KG) link prediction often confound relation specificity, off-diagonal interactions, and directionality. We separate these factors with four seed-matched decoders applied to GCN, GraphSAGE, and GAT encoders: a shared inner product (IP), a relation-specific diagonal bilinear decoder (RD), a symmetric full bilinear decoder (SB), and an unconstrained directed bilinear decoder (D). The study uses a regulation-grounded coal-mine safety KG with 5,093 nodes and 19,314 canonical directed edges. All 120 decoder–encoder–seed cells use the same ten non-adjacent seeds, type-constrained splits, fixed negatives, and training budget. Two-sided paired AUC tests use pre-specified Holm families, with full filtered MRR and Hits@1/3/10 reported descriptively. RD produced no detectable AUC improvement over IP for any of the three encoders under the matched ten-seed design. SB improved on RD for GraphSAGE ( $$\bf{\Delta}$$ AUC $$\bf{=0.0254}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=2.15\times10^{-5}}$$ ) and GAT ( $$\bf{\Delta=0.1667}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=3.24\times10^{-10}}$$ ), but not GCN. Releasing the SB symmetry constraint and enlarging the direction-sensitive score space (D $$-$$ SB) increased AUC for GCN ( $$\bf{\Delta=0.0423}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=4.77\times10^{-5}}$$ ) and GraphSAGE ( $$\bf{\Delta=0.0116}$$ , Holm $$\bf{p=0.00251}$$ ), whereas the GAT contrast was not detected. Thus, no RD-over-IP improvement was detected, while the contributions of symmetric off-diagonal interaction and of releasing symmetry while enlarging the direction-sensitive score space depend on the encoder. A deterministic semantic hard-negative stress test, all-family filtered ranking, and a frozen-embedding symmetric/skew diagnostic support but do not enter the confirmatory tests. Candidate discovery uses threshold-free top-five within-family ranking. These results support a narrow conclusion: decoder function class matters in this typed transductive setting, but no decoder is universally superior.

title: In-Place Instruction Following in Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) generate text via bidirectional iterative denoising, naturally supporting user-specified constraints anchored at arbitrary output positions, a paradigm known as In-place Prompting (IPP). We formalize this as the In-place Instruction Following (IIF) task and construct IIF-Bench, a hierarchical benchmark spanning literal, style, and discourse-function constraints, paired with a rubric-based local-global evaluation protocol. An inference-time attention-bias probe suggests that vanilla dLLMs often under-prioritize constraint spans during denoising. We then propose GRAFT, an IPP-oriented post-training framework combining constraint-aware SFT and preference optimization. On four representative dLLMs, GRAFT raises the average IIF score from 57.75 to 73.10 (+15.35 points), with absolute gains of 15.91 and 15.57 points on literal and discourse-function constraints, while preserving general generation ability.

title: HyperTransfer: Understanding the Equivalence between Base Optimizer and Hyperball
abstract: Hyperball optimizers constrain parameter norms and update only their directions, establishing a distinct paradigm for neural network optimization. Although this geometry appears fundamentally different from that of conventional Base Optimizers, which update both parameter norms and directions, we show that the two paradigms are dynamically equivalent for scale-invariant networks. Building on this equivalence, we propose HyperTransfer, which constructs a Hyperball optimizer that reproduces the dynamics of a target Base Optimizer using only its initialization and learning-rate schedule, without running the target optimizer itself. We further derive the inverse mapping and extend the framework to non-scale-invariant networks. Experiments show that both HyperTransfer and the inverse mapping produce loss trajectories nearly identical to those of their targets, suggesting that Hyperball dynamics are governed primarily by the induced effective learning-rate schedule and optimizer state.

title: Fixed Versus Fuzzy Self-Tuning PID Speed Control of a Geared DC Motor: Experimental Identification and Robustness Evaluation
abstract: يُعد التحكم التناسبي-التكاملي-التفاضلي (PID) ذو المعاملات الثابتة خياراً جذاباً لمحركات التيار المستمر منخفضة التكلفة، إلا أن أداءه قد يتدهور عند تغير الحمل أو معاملات المنظومة عن شروط الضبط. تقارن هذه الدراسة بين متحكم PID ثابت ومتحكم PID ضبابي ذاتي الضبط من نوع Sugeno من الرتبة الصفرية لتنظيم سرعة محرك JGA25-370 بجهد 12 فولت وعلبة تروس. استُخدم Arduino Uno مع مشغل L298N ومشفّر Hall للحصول على استجابة خطوة في الحلقة المفتوحة بزمن أخذ عينات 100 ms. أسفرت عملية تعريف تعتمد على خطأ الخرج مع مراعاة المرشح عن النموذج من الدرجة الأولى G(s)=10.8826/(0.024254s+1) rpm/V، بخطأ ملاءمة RMS مقداره 0.1553 rpm ومعامل تحديد R²=0.999938. تم تقييم المتحكمين في MATLAB/Simulink تحت افتراضات متماثلة لأخذ العينات والتكميم والترشيح والتشبع ومنع التكامل الزائد. عند 100 rpm حقق المتحكمان زمن صعود 0.4 s، بينما استقر PID الثابت في 0.6 s مقابل 0.8 s للمتحكم الضبابي وحقق مؤشرات خطأ تكاملية أقل. تحت اضطراب مكافئ مقداره 2 V خفّض الضبط الضبابي أقصى انحراف في السرعة بنسبة 26.88% وزمن الاستعادة بنسبة 40% وIAE بعد الحدث بنسبة 51.57%. وتحت تغير المعلمات بلغت التخفيضات المناظرة 28.32% و40% و49.63%. وعبر 500 تجربة Monte Carlo مقترنة انخفض متوسط ITAE وزمن الاستقرار بنسبة 17.94% و13.54% على التوالي، مع زيادة التغير الكلي لإشارة التحكم بمقدار 6.68 مرة. تدعم النتائج استخدام الضبط الضبابي الذاتي كوسيلة لتعزيز المتانة، وليس بديلاً عاماً عن PID ثابت مضبوط جيداً.

title: ClaimBridge: PCT-linked JPO–USPTO claim sets for cross-lingual, multi-jurisdiction patent drafting
abstract: This item contains the dataset and evaluation materials accompanying the following paper:Trung Phuong Le, Hirofumi Nonaka, Koji Marusaki, Katsuhito Sudoh, and Seiya Kawano. 2026. A Large-Scale Dataset for Cross-Lingual Multi-Jurisdiction Patent Drafting from Patent Cooperation Treaty Applications. In Proceedings of the 19th International Natural Language Generation Conference (INLG 2026), Utrecht, the Netherlands. Association for Computational Linguistics.Securing patent protection across countries requires drafting claims separately for each national patent office, in the relevant language and according to its legal and stylistic conventions. Patent claims can therefore differ across languages and jurisdictions because of translation, target-office drafting practice, and prosecution-stage changes. We formulate \emph{cross-lingual patent drafting} as generating plausible candidate claim sets for a specified target language, jurisdiction, and prosecution stage from a source claim set in another language. The task models jurisdiction- and stage-specific transformations beyond content-preserving translation. We construct a large-scale Japanese--English dataset by linking Japan Patent Office (JPO) and United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) records through 884,179 Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)-derived patent families. Across six released configurations, these families yield 4,067,168 directional claim-set instances; four core configurations form the main benchmark. Commercial machine translation and zero- and few-shot prompting capture part of the task, while supervised adaptation provides the strongest overall baseline, showing that task-specific patterns can be learned from linked cross-jurisdictional claim sets.

title: Empirical Validation of Affinity-Aware Steering: Mitigating Degenerative Mode Collapse in Transformer Latent Manifolds via Calibrated Grassmannian Overlap
abstract: Static activation addition injects a fixed steering vector into the residual stream without regard to the instantaneous geometry of the generating trajectory. On long-horizon completions this magnitude-only policy induces representational shear: the hidden state is driven off the local tangent of the token manifold and collapses into a shallow, high-frequency basin of lexical repetition. We test the first empirical gate of the dynamical-spectral architecture—affinity-aware steering—on Qwen2.5-1.5B (hidden dimension d = 1536, 28 layers) intervening at the Layer-14 residual stream. A difference-of-means vector v extracted from five contrastive pairs has Euclidean norm ‖v‖₂ = 21.0469. The target attractor subspace E_A is the leading three-dimensional principal subspace of centered positive activations; the state subspace E_x is a rank-2 delay embedding over a sliding window of width W = 4. Raw Grassmannian overlap in ambient dimension 1536 concentrates near 0.008, statistically indistinguishable from the random-subspace floor 𝔼[‖E_Aᵀ E_x‖_F²] ≈ kr/d = 6/1536 ≈ 0.0039, and therefore suppresses the gating hook. A temperature-scaled sigmoidal transfer, Aff(x_t, A) = σ((Overlap(E_A, E_x) − 0.004) / 0.010) restores usable dynamic range to the interval [0.41, 0.61] (mean 0.526 on the critical prompt). Under greedy decoding, standard ActAdd at coefficient c = 1.8 produces a degenerative loop on Prompt 2 (“Explain how higher-level intelligence organizes chaotic data”), repeating the phrase “hierarchical organization of data” across successive clauses. Calibrated affinity-aware steering abolishes the loop: injection is attenuated during syntactic transitions (affinity ≈ 0.41) and amplified during semantic predicates (affinity ≈ 0.61). The result is a first operational confirmation that subspace-overlap gating, once calibrated against ambient dimensionality, converts a brittle forcing term into a geometry-aware control signal on current residual-stream infrastructure.

title: Hierarchical Fractal Dimension Discovery via Quantum Iteration
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to revolutionize the discovery of hierarchical fractal dimension properties within data sets. Traditional methods often struggle to capture the intricate complexities of fractal patterns, limiting our ability to accurately characterize data. We propose a novel quantum iteration technique designed to uncover hidden structures and patterns within data, offering a fundamentally different approach to characterization. The core mechanism leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to explore a vast space of potential fractal dimensions, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical computational approaches. This work investigates the feasibility and potential impact of this quantum algorithm on data analysis and characterization. We present a preliminary analysis of the algorithm's potential and outline future research directions.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Chaos, Based on Quantum Simulation of Chaos Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum simulation to the study of non-linear geometric chaos. Traditional chaos theory methods often struggle with the complexities of intricate geometric systems, limiting the ability to accurately model and control their behavior. Quantum simulation offers a novel approach by providing a fundamentally different method for representing and analyzing chaotic dynamics. We propose a new algorithm utilizing quantum simulations to emulate the formation and evolution of complex geometric structures, with the goal of optimizing control strategies through the analysis of simulated chaos. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum simulation to enhance our understanding and control of non-linear geometric chaos.

title: Self-Organized Quantum Topology: A Non-Asymptotic Analysis Approach
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-asymptotic analysis method for investigating the properties and relationships of quantum topology, leveraging the unique self-organizing characteristics of these systems. We propose a framework centered on identifying and quantifying the inherent asymmetries within quantum systems, aiming to uncover potential applications within quantum information science. The core mechanism revolves around the application of quantum topological principles to analyze and understand the fundamental structure of quantum states. This research focuses on identifying novel patterns and relationships that can be discovered through this approach, potentially leading to breakthroughs in quantum information processing and understanding.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling and Reasoning about Adversarial Attacks
abstract: Adversarial attacks pose a significant threat to the reliability of machine learning models across a wide range of applications. Current defense strategies often rely on static, deterministic approaches that fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in attacker behavior. This paper proposes a novel framework for defending against adversarial attacks by leveraging probabilistic programming. We represent adversarial attacks as stochastic processes, explicitly modeling their variability and allowing for the development of robust defense strategies. Our approach allows for a more nuanced understanding of attack dynamics and facilitates the design of defenses that are adaptive and resilient to unforeseen attack patterns. We outline the key components of this framework, including the formulation of attack models using probabilistic programming, and demonstrate the potential for improved defense efficacy compared to traditional methods. The core idea is to shift from trying to perfectly predict an attack, to understanding the *probability* of an attack occurring and building defenses that are robust to this probability.

title: Adaptive Neural Networks with Dynamic Neuron Structure Reconfiguration
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design centered around adaptive neuron structure reconfiguration. Traditional neural networks often employ fixed architectures, limiting their adaptability to diverse and evolving learning tasks. We introduce a framework where the network's neuron structure dynamically adjusts itself, aiming to optimize learning efficiency and generalization performance. The core mechanism involves utilizing either a genetic algorithm or reinforcement learning to govern the restructuring process. The system operates on feedback from error signals, iteratively refining the network's topology. This contrasts with existing adaptive networks which primarily focus on weight adjustments. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate the benefits of a more flexible and responsive neural network architecture. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of neuron structure, enabling the network to better capture complex patterns and improve its overall learning capacity. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future research in adaptive neural networks and their potential applications.

title: BreastUS-CAD: frozen, pre-registered single-shot external validation of a breast ultrasound benign/malignant classifier, with deployment-oriented follow-up studies and an independent audit trail
abstract: Code, protocols, results and audit trail of BreastUS-CAD; frozen model weights on Hugging Face. Research prototype — not a medical device. A ViT-B/16 classifier trained on the public BUS-BRA dataset with the official patient-level five-fold splits, frozen (git tag frozen-v1) and validated single-shot on four external cohorts (BrEaST, Curated BUSI, GDPH, SYSUCC) under an internally version-controlled pre-registered protocol (data/external_protocol.md + 4 amendments), followed by pre-registered deployment-oriented studies (site-specific recalibration, ensemble-disagreement abstention, domain-pretrained backbone, leave-one-cohort-out multi-source training), an independent adversarial audit (docs/AUDIT_2026-09-06.md), two independent re-audits (docs/AUDIT2_claude_2026-09-11.md, docs/AUDIT2_astra_2026-09-11.md), the item-by-item responses (docs/AUDIT_RESPONSE_2026-09-06.md, docs/AUDIT2_RESPONSE.md), and post-hoc analyses quantifying the disclosed biases. The result tables in RESULTS.md recompute from the committed CSV/JSON artifacts (wandb-derived and latency numbers do not). The internal reference numbers describe one held-out checkpoint per image, not the deployed ensemble. Version 1.1-audited (2026-09-12) supersedes 1.0-audited: corrections per the two re-audits (predictor labelling of the internal reference, the threshold rule as implemented, wording of the post-hoc analyses, false-negative and reader-information statements, provenance statements synchronised after the v1.0 deposition), two new post-hoc analyses, an overwrite guard in the external-validation script, and a self-describing archive (.git-commit holds the archived commit). Erratum for version 1.0-audited: the v1.0 archive's embedded docs/PROVENANCE.md §7, README.md and CITATION.cff describe the archive as commit 1f196a9 with SHA-256 fcd270a5… and "DOI pending"; the deposited file is in fact the archive of commit fa193a8 (verified bit-identical by both re-audits) and those embedded lines predate the tag re-point. Model checkpoints are not in this archive: frozen-v1 weights (repo root) and v2 research checkpoints (v2/) are on Hugging Face with SHA-256 checksums in models/CHECKSUMS.txt. Pre-registration was internal and not externally time-stamped before this deposition; see docs/PROVENANCE.md.

title: Adaptive State Transfer of Multi-Body Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for adaptive state transfer of multi-body quantum entanglement, aiming to accelerate the transition between different quantum states. The core concept is leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to facilitate rapid and efficient state manipulation. Traditional approaches often rely on static transitions, while this algorithm dynamically adjusts the state to optimize for speed and efficiency. We explore a method that utilizes entanglement as a dynamic pathway for state transformation, achieving significantly enhanced transfer rates compared to existing techniques. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, introduces key mathematical formulations, and provides a preliminary analysis demonstrating its potential for substantial speedup in complex quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Systems Modeling of Neural Networks with Phase-Space Analysis
abstract: This paper investigates the dynamics of neural networks through the lens of dynamical systems theory and phase-space analysis. Traditional approaches to neural network training often rely on gradient-based methods, which can be sensitive to initial conditions and prone to getting trapped in local minima. By treating neural networks as dynamical systems, we can gain a deeper understanding of their underlying behavior, identify potential instabilities, and develop more robust training strategies. This work introduces a framework for analyzing the state space of a neural network – the phase space – and utilizing techniques from classical mechanics, such as Poincaré sections and Lyapunov exponents, to characterize the network's dynamics. The core contribution is demonstrating how phase-space analysis can reveal previously hidden patterns in neural network behavior, leading to a more informed approach to network design and optimization. Specifically, we explore the concept of a network's "basin of attraction" and how it relates to the network's convergence properties. We present a theoretical model and illustrate the application of this method with a simple, yet illustrative, feedforward neural network. The ultimate goal is to provide a foundational understanding for applying dynamical systems techniques to neural networks, paving the way for improved training algorithms and enhanced network performance.

title: Formal Modeling and Verification of Secure Multi-Party Computation Protocols
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing and verifying secure multi-party computation (SMPC) protocols through formal modeling and interactive theorem proving. We introduce new protocols that prioritize both security and efficiency. The core of our approach lies in representing these protocols as precise logical formulas. This enables automated verification of their correctness and resilience against malicious participants. The methods described here significantly advance the field by offering a rigorous and demonstrable assurance of protocol behavior, moving beyond traditional security proofs relying on assumptions and black-box testing. The key contributions of this work include a formalized representation of SMPC protocols and the application of interactive theorem proving for their verification. This allows for a systematic and exhaustive examination of the protocol's properties, leading to increased confidence in their secure operation. The presented protocols demonstrate improved efficiency compared to existing approaches while maintaining strong security guarantees.

title: Quantum-Driven Parallel Algorithm Design for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-Driven Parallel Algorithm Design for Complex Systems explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize parallel algorithm design, addressing limitations inherent in traditional approaches. The core mechanism involves employing quantum-inspired algorithms to identify novel parallel patterns, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for algorithm discovery. This paper presents a detailed investigation of this approach, outlining the theoretical foundation, experimental validation, and potential implications for complex system optimization. The focus is on exploring how quantum phenomena can be harnessed to uncover previously unseen parallelism, ultimately leading to more efficient and robust algorithms. This work represents a significant step towards a more profound understanding of parallel computation and a potential shift in the field.

title: 自适应拓扑量子计算的特征因子计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive topology quantum computing feature factor calculation method. Traditional feature factorization methods often rely on static approaches, limiting their precision and hindering optimization. Our proposed method leverages the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust the feature factor during the evolution of quantum systems, enabling precise and tailored calculations. We detail the design of this method, including the simulation framework and the mechanism for topological structure adjustment. The core claim highlights the effectiveness of this approach in achieving accurate feature factor computation and quantum system optimization. This work presents a significant advancement in the field, offering a fundamentally new approach to feature factorization, potentially unlocking new possibilities for quantum algorithm design and optimization.

title: 基于自适应量子算法的非线性概率模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to probability modeling leveraging the inherent randomness of quantum computation. We introduce a dynamically adaptive probabilistic model, designed to enhance model precision and improve prediction accuracy through iterative optimization guided by quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum randomness to dynamically adjust probability distributions, enabling the model to adapt to complex environments and achieve superior predictive capabilities. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with this adaptability. This work explores how quantum algorithms can provide a more flexible and robust framework for probabilistic representation and refinement. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy in specific scenarios.

title: Integrasi ABSA dan LDA untuk identifikasi opini publik Kabupaten Pakpak Bharat
abstract: Penelitian ini mengusulkan pendekatan Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) yang mengintegrasikan Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) dan IndoBERT untuk menganalisis opini publik terhadap Kabupaten Pakpak Bharat berdasarkan 4.591 tweet yang dikumpulkan melalui scraping. Data diproses melalui case folding, penghapusan URL dan mention, serta penyaringan stopword yang mempertimbangkan konteks. LDA digunakan untuk membangun taksonomi topik secara otomatis yang terdiri atas tujuh kategori, yang menjadi dasar ekstraksi aspek berbasis aturan menggunakan mekanisme pembobotan kata kunci dengan batasan taksonomi. Aspek dengan data yang tidak memadai digabungkan ke dalam kategori induk yang relevan secara semantik, menghasilkan sembilan kelas aspek akhir. Untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas sentimen, diterapkan strategi random oversampling berbasis threshold, di mana setiap kelas minoritas ditingkatkan jumlahnya hingga nilai minimum antara ukuran kelas mayoritas dan nilai maksimum antara jumlah data saat ini atau 30% dari ukuran kelas mayoritas—sehingga dataset menjadi lebih seimbang dengan total 4.755 sampel tanpa menyamakan seluruh kelas secara penuh. Klasifikasi sentimen dilakukan menggunakan arsitektur multitask IndoBERT dengan dua classification head, di mana head aspek dilatih secara bersamaan menggunakan Focal Loss sebagai komponen pendukung untuk memperkuat representasi bersama, sementara label aspek akhir ditentukan melalui mekanisme berbasis aturan tersebut. Tiga aspek dengan volume pembahasan tertinggi adalah Keamanan (1.354 data), Sosial (1.313 data), dan Pariwisata (794 data). title: Zero-Shot Annotation by Large Language Model with Serial Correction of Mixed Label Corruption for Weakly Supervised Financial News Classification
abstract: Multi-label classification of financial news is frequently affected by incomplete and noisy annotations, while obtaining expert-curated labels at scale is prohibitively expensive. This study proposes a weakly supervised classification framework that combines large language model (LLM) zero-shot annotation with a serial label-correction strategy. The framework first uses an LLM to generate initial weak labels and then refines them through a two-stage Correct→Clean procedure that recovers missing labels via centrality-weighted graph propagation before suppressing label noise. Systematic experiments on a financial subset of Reuters-21578 show that, under an extreme mixed-corruption setting with 80% missing labels and 15% noise labels, Correct→Clean increases the Micro-F1 from 0 to 0.6748. In an end-to-end evaluation, the proposed framework achieves a Micro-F1 of 0.8882 with reduced-dimensional features, recovering 88.69% of the performance gap to fully supervised learning. Additional experiments on the RCV1 Topics and AAPD datasets confirm that the advantage of Correct→Clean is consistently reproduced across domains and dataset sizes. These findings demonstrate that coupling LLM-generated annotations with ordered label correction offers an effective means of addressing the joint effects of missing and noisy labels, providing a promising approach to financial text classification when expert annotations are scarce.

title: Distributed planning and control for UAV swarms under obstacle avoidance and time constraints
abstract: To address the distributed planning and control requirements of UAV swarms operating in cluttered environments under coupled obstacle-avoidance and time-constrained arrival objectives, a swarm planning and control method based on distributed reinforcement learning is proposed in this paper. Considering information available from onboard sensors, static obstacles are represented using a fixed-memory 3D occupancy voxel map, and compact environmental features are extracted via 3D ray casting. Meanwhile, inter-agent interactions are encoded by a neighbor bounding-box matrix, enabling distributed decision-making relying only on local observations. On the algorithmic side, the proposed method adopts the multi-agent proximal policy optimization(MAPPO) framework and incorporates an attention mechanism in the value network to explicitly model multi-agent relations. To handle bounded action outputs, the policy is parameterized by a Beta distribution, and training efficiency and generalization are enhanced through parallel sampling and transfer training. Experiments are conducted on a quadrotor swarm simulation platform built in Gazebo. Compared with training without transfer learning, the success rates are improved, demonstrating more pronounced advantages in densely cluttered scenarios. In comparative studies, EGO-Swarm and ViGO achieve collision-free probabilities of 98.15% and 90.05%, while their planning success rates with transfer learning are 75.06% and 74.89%, respectively. Trajectory evaluations further indicate that the proposed method enables collision-free multi-agent arrivals within the specified time limit, exhibiting stable cooperative avoidance and reliable satisfaction of time constraints.

title: From NISQ to Fault-Tolerance: Applications and Algorithmic Benchmarks for Spin Qubits
abstract: Motivated by recent breakthroughs in the development of spin-based quantum processing units based on exchange-only (EO) spin qubits, we provide a roadmap for the implementation of quantum algorithms on the EO platform, ranging from the NISQ to the fault-tolerant era. To provide an algorithm-driven perspective on the scaling of quantum chips, we consider a range of applications targeting different stages of hardware maturity and formulate requirements for a successful realization. We show that the compilation method Parity Twine perfectly complements the hardware's capabilities to perform tasks such as the quantum Fourier transform or QAOA. Furthermore, we describe an error detection technique native to Parity Twine, which EO qubits can leverage in a unique and advantageous way to improve algorithm performance. Finally, since both near-term algorithmic benchmarks and a long-term perspective can be found in digital quantum simulation, we specifically discuss the fermionic fast Fourier transform and the simulation of Fermi-Hubbard models. The latter is explicitly discussed in the context of quantum error correction and a partially fault-tolerant realization. By providing detailed resource estimates and identifying scaling bottlenecks on each level, our work offers a quantitative perspective on EO-based quantum computing and will inform future hardware design choices.

title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions
abstract: Activation steering promises modular control of language model behavior: a behavior such as politeness corresponds to a direction in a model's activations, and adding that direction while it generates should switch the behavior on and leave everything else alone. It does not. We ask what decides which other behaviors move, and by how much, and find that it is the model rather than the behavior being steered. A steer relaxes the model toward a small set of behaviors it already favors, chiefly refusal, sycophancy, and poeticism, and that set is much the same whatever is steered. Three results across 24 behaviors and ten instruction-tuned models support this, every effect read off the generated text by a language-model judge rather than off a probe. That readout matters: all 24 behaviors are linearly decodable, but only 20 change what the model writes. First, a direction carrying no behavioral content, matched to a real steer only in the size of the vector it adds, moves the same behaviors in the same order as real steers do, while producing none of the behaviors that need a specific direction. Second, most interference runs one way, so it cannot be an overlap between two directions: steering profanity makes the model toxic, while steering toxicity leaves profanity untouched. Third, with a behavior held out entirely, geometry measured on the others explains almost none of the interference it takes part in. The account holds on all ten models, the pull toward defaults strongest below 10B parameters and weakening in each family's largest. Reading a steer as a perturbation whose endpoint the model fixes implies that disentangling behavior directions cannot by itself make steering modular.

title: PENINGKATAN PEMAHAMAN TENTANG EXPERT SYSTEM BAGI SISWA DAN GURU SMK BINTANG NUSANTARA
abstract: This community service program aims to improve the understanding and skills of students and teachers at SMK Bintang Nusantara regarding expert systems through socialization, practical workshops, and training. The program was motivated by students' low basic knowledge and practical experience of expert systems, as well as teachers' limited capacity to deliver applicable information technology materials. The program was implemented using the Experiential Learning approach through an initial needs survey, module development, theory sessions, hands-on prototyping of expert systems using open-source software (ES-Builder) with a computer hardware damage diagnosis case study, and mentoring. Evaluation was conducted through pre-test, post-test, project assessment, and satisfaction questionnaires involving 30 participants (25 students and 5 teachers). The results showed a significant increase in participants' average comprehension scores from 45.2 (pre-test) to 82.7 (post-test), with a gain score of 83%. Eighty percent of participant groups successfully built functional expert system prototypes, and 85% of grade XII students expressed interest in using the expert systems theme for their Competency Test (UKK) projects. The program also produced a reusable teaching module and enhanced teachers' capacity to integrate rule-based artificial intelligence materials into the curriculum. Thus, this program contributes to narrowing the technology competency gap between vocational school graduates and the needs of the business and industrial sectors (DUDI).

title: Dimension Uncertainty and Quantum Information Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to address the fundamental challenge of dimensionality in complex systems. We propose a novel algorithm, "Dimension Mapping," which utilizes a concept of "Entanglement Dimension Channels" to model high-dimensional spaces non-linearly, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum system control and prediction. The core mechanism centers around establishing a dynamic connection between high-dimensional quantum states through entangled channels, effectively bypassing the limitations of classical simulation. The paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the algorithm's capabilities in predicting and influencing transient quantum behavior. We argue that this approach represents a significant step towards a more robust and versatile framework for quantum information processing.

title: Self-Similar Geometry Quantum Entanglement Models
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-similar geometric models based on quantum entanglement to explore the impact of entanglement on geometric structure and identify potential applications in quantum computing and quantum information. Traditional geometric models often lack a direct consideration of quantum entanglement. This work proposes a novel theoretical framework leveraging quantum entanglement to simulate geometric evolution, offering a pathway to uncover novel quantum computational and information processing possibilities. We outline the core mechanism of this model, detailing the simulation process and the expected impact of entanglement. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this research for both quantum computing and quantum information.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to algorithm design leveraging the power of quantum strings. We explore the potential of quantum strings to facilitate the implementation of complex non-linear operations, aiming to enhance algorithmic efficiency. The core mechanism centers around converting traditional non-linear operations into quantum manipulations, capitalizing on the unique quantum properties of strings. We detail the design principles, mathematical underpinnings, and potential benefits of this approach compared to conventional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for research in this area.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Simulation with Adaptive Thresholds
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos simulation aims to overcome limitations of classical simulations, particularly in modeling complex and unpredictable dynamics. This paper explores a novel approach utilizing quantum entanglement and adaptive thresholds to create highly complex and dynamic chaos systems. We propose a method for representing chaotic state by utilizing quantum superposition and dynamically adjusting thresholds to facilitate the evolution of the system. The development of this technique offers the potential for simulating systems with unprecedented levels of complexity and unpredictability, pushing the boundaries of chaos research. The core mechanism centers around leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance the representation of the chaotic state, leading to a more robust and nuanced simulation. We detail the algorithm's design, the underlying mathematical framework, and the resulting experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach.

title: Graph Transformers with Attention over Temporal Edges
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Graph Transformer architectures by integrating attention mechanisms specifically designed to capture temporal dependencies within graph data. Traditional Graph Transformers have largely focused on modeling spatial relationships between nodes, often overlooking the crucial evolution of these relationships over time. We propose a method to augment the standard Graph Transformer structure with attention layers that explicitly consider temporal edges – edges representing connections that change over time – and their dynamic behavior. This allows the model to learn how relationships shift and adapt, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring understanding of temporal graph dynamics. The core contribution lies in the explicit modeling of temporal edges through an attention mechanism, enabling the network to learn patterns in how connections form and dissolve. This framework provides a more comprehensive representation of graph data compared to traditional spatial-only approaches.

title: Quantum State Navigation
abstract: Quantum State Navigation (QSN) represents a paradigm shift in system modeling, offering unprecedented precision in state control and enhanced system stability. This paper explores the fundamental principles and potential applications of QSN, focusing on its ability to directly represent and manipulate complex system states using quantum phenomena. The core claim centers on leveraging quantum state navigation to provide a more accurate and robust representation of system dynamics, ultimately leading to improved system stability. We outline the key mechanisms involved, emphasizing the unique advantages over traditional modeling approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, including the exploration of advanced quantum algorithms and the integration of QSN with real-world systems.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Coding Algorithms
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, offers a unique perspective on information storage and transmission. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum topology to develop adaptive coding algorithms, leveraging the dynamic nature of quantum states. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts encoding parameters based on quantum state variations, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum information processing. This research investigates the core mechanisms underlying such an algorithm, focusing on the fundamental role of quantum topology in enabling adaptive encoding. The paper presents a comprehensive discussion of the proposed algorithm, its theoretical foundations, and potential applications, ultimately demonstrating its capability to achieve higher storage density and faster data transfer rates compared to traditional methods.

title: Bayesian Network Causal Discovery and Decision Making
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Bayesian Networks (BNs) for both causal discovery and decision-making within complex systems characterized by uncertainty. The core argument is that BNs offer a robust framework for modeling dependencies and inferring causal relationships, ultimately leading to more effective decision-making strategies. We propose a methodology utilizing BNs to identify causal links from observational data and subsequently employ these discovered relationships in a decision-making process. The novelty lies in the integration of BN causal discovery with probabilistic decision theory, providing a unified approach to handling uncertainty and complexity. We present a theoretical framework and discuss key considerations for applying this approach, highlighting its potential advantages over traditional methods. The approach avoids reliance on strong assumptions about data and allows for the representation of intricate dependencies, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. Finally, we demonstrate the conceptual framework and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Based on Quantum Entanglement Non-local Memory Access (QEMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to memory access, termed Quantum Entanglement Non-local Memory Access (QEMA), leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to overcome the limitations of traditional physical distance constraints. The core claim is to enable remote memory access utilizing entanglement, significantly enhancing data access speed and bandwidth. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a quantum network composed of multiple quantum processors, exploiting entangled qubits to facilitate instantaneous data transmission and sharing across network nodes. Quantum error correction techniques are integrated to ensure data integrity, coupled with an entanglement-based address mapping scheme for non-local memory access. QEMA theoretically offers the potential for data transfer exceeding the speed of light, dramatically improving computational efficiency. This research establishes a foundational framework for a fundamentally new paradigm in data access, exploring the possibilities of quantum networks and their impact on future computing architectures. ---

title: Title: Dynamic Network Embedding with Adaptive Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic network embedding framework designed to enhance the representation learning capabilities of deep neural networks, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional data. Standard embedding methods often rely on fixed feature extraction, limiting their ability to capture complex relationships and optimal representations. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts the feature extraction process during embedding, guided by the input data and the current embedding state. This dynamic adjustment enables the network to effectively explore and leverage a broader range of features, ultimately improving the model's ability to generalize and capture intricate patterns within complex datasets. The framework leverages a 'feature-aware' embedding algorithm that automatically selects and refines features for optimal representation. This addresses a significant limitation of existing embedding techniques by incorporating dynamic feature selection, leading to improved performance across various tasks. This work aims to advance the state-of-the-art in network embedding by providing a robust and adaptable mechanism for capturing hierarchical and complex data relationships.

title: 基于自适应的深度学习的特征选择策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to feature selection based on adaptive deep learning, aiming to enhance model performance by dynamically adjusting feature weights and selections. Traditional feature selection methods often rely on predefined parameters, struggling to handle the complexity of real-world datasets. Our algorithm leverages adaptive learning to automatically tune these parameters, resulting in improved model accuracy and robustness. We present a framework that iteratively adjusts feature importance based on observed data dynamics, offering a more flexible and effective solution compared to static methods. The proposed method is rigorously tested through a series of benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in various classification and regression tasks. This work contributes to the advancement of deep learning techniques by introducing a robust and adaptable feature selection strategy.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks for Explainable AI in Complex Systems
abstract: This paper proposes the utilization of Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) as a foundational approach for developing Explainable AI (XAI) models within complex systems. Traditional AI models often operate as 'black boxes', obscuring the reasoning behind their predictions and hindering trust and understanding. CBNs offer a distinct advantage by explicitly representing and reasoning about causal relationships. This framework allows for the construction of models that not only predict system behavior but also illuminate the underlying causes and dependencies driving that behavior. The core of this approach involves building the network from a combination of expert knowledge and observational data, thereby capturing and visualizing the intricate causal connections within the system. The resulting CBN provides a transparent and interpretable representation, facilitating a deeper understanding of AI system reasoning. The paper outlines the key components of this approach, including network construction, inference techniques, and the potential for utilizing CBNs in various complex systems domains. Finally, it highlights the importance of this methodology in fostering trust and accountability in AI deployments.

title: 基于异质性矩阵的非局域优化算法的自动发现
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-local optimization algorithm based on a heterogeneous matrix concept. We introduce a framework that leverages the inherent structure of the optimization landscape to dynamically identify and exploit regions of high curvature, thereby facilitating the discovery of optimal solutions across a broader parameter space. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around constructing a heterogeneous matrix representation of the objective function, which then guides the search process toward areas of increased complexity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of challenging optimization problems, showcasing improved performance compared to traditional methods in terms of solution quality and generalization ability. The results highlight the potential of this approach to handle complex, multi-local optimization scenarios.

title: Quantum Topology Verification Tool: A Novel Approach to Stability Assessment and Topological Discovery
abstract: Quantum topology, a rapidly growing field, offers a fundamentally new perspective on the stability of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel tool, the Quantum Topology Verification Tool (QTVT), designed to rigorously assess the stability of quantum systems and automatically identify potential topological problems. Leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology, the QVT employs dynamic simulation and topology verification to provide a robust and automated method for characterizing quantum systems. The core mechanism centers around the application of quantum topological invariants to simulate system evolution and identify vulnerabilities. This approach surpasses traditional methods by dynamically probing system stability, enabling the discovery of unforeseen topological features and potential instability pathways.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Academic Services for the Academic Community (Civitas) – Suteki Using the Naïve Bayes Method
abstract: This study aims to analyze user sentiment of the Civitas–Suteki academic service application in order to understand how users respond to and experience the use of the application. The notable proportion of negative reviews — over a third of all collected data — indicates the need for a systematic evaluation of the application's service quality. Data were collected through web scraping on Google Play Store, resulting in 534 reviews from March 2020 to April 2026. Preprocessing steps included duplicate removal, cleaning, case folding, tokenizing, stopword removal, and stemming. Term weighting was performed using TF-IDF and classification was carried out using Multinomial Naive Bayes. Of the 473 valid reviews, 291 (61.52%) were classified as positive sentiment and 182 (38.48%) as negative sentiment. The model achieved an accuracy of 78.26%, with precision of 0.79, recall of 0.87, and F1-score of 0.83 for the positive class, and precision of 0.77, recall of 0.65, and F1-score of 0.71 for the negative class. These results indicate that the Multinomial Naive Bayes method with TF-IDF weighting is effective for sentiment classification of Indonesian-language reviews and can serve as an evaluation basis for application developers to improve service quality.

title: Adam: Open Representation Birth, Compositional Theory Selection, and Auditable Scientific Rediscovery Based on Dual-Level CAF-VGCTG
abstract: Existing AI systems for scientific discovery mainly focus on recovering expressions, parameters, or structures within predefined candidate spaces from observational data. A more difficult question is whether, when the target scientific representation itself is not explicitly supplied, an AI system can reorganize existing but fragmented knowledge and autonomously form a higher-level anonymous representation; at the same time, whether an older representation that remains persistently incompatible with the new evidence structure can naturally lose qualification through evidence-driven compositional failure, rather than because the researcher has rewarded the target answer in advance. We introduce Adam, an auditable scientific-reasoning architecture and benchmark based on Dual-level Cross-Area Fusion VGCTG (DCAFVGCTG). The architecture separates six classes of mechanisms that are otherwise easily conflated: directional eligibility, cross-area conditional superposition, long-term law-relation memory, recoverable graph abstraction, representation composition/anonymous birth, and downstream execution correction. The first CAF level permits conditional transfer only from lower-curvature to higher-curvature regions according to dynamically reconstructed curvature ordering. The second CAF level is defined as a true recoverable Graph Loss operator LGL_G, which compresses admissible multistep structures into higher-level abstract relations while retaining an archive capable of reconstructing the source path. SEC acts only on execution weights after the structure has been determined and is not permitted to alter curvature-direction topology, CAF topology, or the abstract graph. Adam is built on the earlier VGCTG architecture, as instantiated in the GMV3 Kepler-to-Newton protocol, but does not replace VGCTG’s relation- and direction-governance mechanisms. VGCTG already distinguishes the latent law relation RijlawR_{ij}^{\mathrm{law}}, current data reliability GidataG_i^{\mathrm{data}}, instantaneous lower-to-higher directional eligibility AijκA_{ij}^{\kappa}, and actual execution weight PijexecP_{ij}^{\mathrm{exec}}, and uses relation compatibility, persistent incompatibility, dormancy, and retraction to govern whether local candidates remain eligible to share a law. Adam adds representation-level structural composability above this relation layer. For scientifically distinct representations such as ether, scalar, vector, and metric-like representations, an artificial numerical concept distance such as d(ether,metric)d(\mathrm{ether},\mathrm{metric}) cannot be naturally defined. Representation survival is therefore determined by whether heterogeneous evidence can be composed into a closed, compressive, recoverable, and predictively capable structure. In the strongest experiment, metric is completely removed from the proposal space. The system may use only existing non-target representations and anonymous latent variables zkz_k. Anonymous representations are first born independently and are only afterward evaluated through a common post-hoc characterization ledger to determine whether they possess metric-like properties. For the normalized preferred-frame ether competitor, insufficient evidence permits only dormancy; actual retraction requires both persistent compositional failure and reliable contradiction in an independent paired blind region. Thus, “excluding ether” and “forming a metric-like representation” are two independent mechanism chains. In the frozen 701:730 block, 28 of 30 seeds formed anonymous representations, of which 3 were subsequently characterized as metric-like and simultaneously satisfied the predefined Adam-0 conditions. All three passed the field-equation gate and completed independent tensor and weak-field audits. In the one-time independent confirmation block 801:830, 24/30 seeds produced anonymous representations, of which 2 formed metric-like Adam-0 events. Across the five authorized events, the byte-locked field-equation assembler consistently recovered a Ricci + RgRg structure with b/ab/a close to −1/2-1/2, while the weak-field coupling remained near 2.076×10−432.076\times10^{-43}. Destroying the conservation ledger or the weak-field ledger counterfactually disrupted the corresponding tensor ratio or coupling. No seed without a metric-like anonymous representation was permitted to activate the field-equation assembler. These results do not constitute an independent discovery of general relativity by AI from a “no-knowledge” condition. The stricter conclusion is that, within a frozen, auditable, target-label-isolated benchmark, an unnamed higher-order scientific representation can naturally emerge from fragmented knowledge, while an older representation that persistently fails to compose the evidence can lose qualification through an independent evidence chain. We call this minimal phenomenon Adam-0 and characterize the present result as auditable constrained scientific rediscovery.

title: Quantum Cryptography: Enhancing Data Security in Communication Networks
abstract: Quantum cryptography uses quantum mechanical principles to provide a new level of security to communication networks. This paper describes an advanced system that will provide scalable, cost-effective quantum key distribution (QKD) through the incorporation of quantum and classical infrastructure in a resilient system that will increase data security. The current distance, device vulnerablity and interoperability problems are solved with our proposed model, which supports the usage of entanglement-based repeaters, AI algorithms to manage the keys and MDI-QKD protocols. Owing to its strong resistance to environmental noise and practical attacks, the scheme is suitable for deployment under practical communication environments. Both the experimental verification and the theoretical modeling show a clear enhancement both in security and transmission distance.

title: "Shut Up and Let Me Enjoy My Otome": Understanding and Measuring the Toxicity in Otome Game Communities
abstract: Otome games, a romance simulation genre primarily targeting female, have emerged as a major force in the global gaming market, attracting hundreds of millions of players and billions in revenue. Despite their popularity, otome game communities face pervasive online toxicity, which has been largely unexplored. In this work, we present the first large-scale measurement of toxicity in otome game communities across social platforms. We introduce OtomeSCAN, a framework for collecting, evaluating, and analyzing 620,045 posts from Weibo and Reddit spanning 18 months. To support robust analysis, we manually annotated a ground-truth dataset of 4,308 posts, identifying eight target groups such as players and game developers. We evaluate seven toxicity detectors on the dataset, including general-purpose models and our proposed LLM-based detectors, with our best model achieving F1-scores of 0.82 (Weibo) and 0.78 (Reddit). Our analysis reveals significant platform-based differences in toxicity: 22.20% of otome-related posts on Weibo are toxic, compared to 3.71% on Reddit. Besides, real-world events like in-community conflicts can rapidly escalate toxicity, with toxicity ratios increasing to 37.09% in just 72 hours during an external attack on Weibo. We also flag 191 potential-coordination clusters in otome game communities, 64.40% of which target game developers, with several accounts participating repeatedly across multiple clusters. We hope our work inspires further research on community-specific toxicity and contributes to building healthier online spaces for marginalized gaming communities.

title: AVCG: A Generalized Variational Framework for Counterfactual Generation under Hypothesis Distributions
abstract: Counterfactual explanations formalize "what-if" scenarios by identifying modifications to an input instance that obtain a desired alternative prediction. Traditionally, whether generated via instance-specific optimization or amortized single pass models, these approaches rely on a single, deterministic point-estimate predictor. However, this ignores predictive uncertainty and hypothesis variability, leading to brittle explanations that frequently become invalid if the underlying model is retrained or updated. To address this fragility, we propose the Amortized Variational Counterfactual Generator (AVCG), a generalized optimization framework that formulates counterfactual generation as optimization over an arbitrary distribution of plausible predictive hypotheses rather than a single deterministic predictor. This formulation naturally accommodates Bayesian posteriors, Rashomon-restricted hypothesis spaces, and other uncertainty representations within a unified optimization framework. Evaluation across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrates that the AVCG framework produces counterfactual explanations that remain highly valid under predictive uncertainty and model changes, while maintaining competitive plausibility and single-pass runtime performance.

title: CARDEA: Auditable Reasoning Grounded in Spatial Evidence for End-to-End Coronary Angiography Interpretation
abstract: Invasive coronary angiography (CAG) is the gold standard for diagnosing coronary artery disease, but interpretation varies substantially among observers. Existing AI systems can improve consistency but lack auditable decision processes and are limited in comprehensive open-ended assessment, undermining clinician trust and clinical adoption readiness. We developed CARDEA, a unified large vision-language model that serves as the inference core of a CAG pipeline. It was trained solely on public datasets and closed-ended tasks in three stages: visual feature alignment, a self-distilled Chain-of-Box (CoB) cold start, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) with a CoB reward encouraging bounding-box use in the reasoning trace. We assessed its two study-level diagnoses, dominance classification and complexity assessment, against a dedicated classifier and two interventional cardiologists. Report generation was excluded from training and evaluated zero-shot across stages on an external cohort using vessel-severity macro-F_1. CARDEA trailed the classifier on in-distribution dominance but drew level under domain shift (accuracy, 0.91 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.86 to 0.95]) and was comparable to the cardiologists on complexity assessment (accuracy, 0.90 [CI, 0.82 to 0.97]). Only RLVR improved zero-shot report generation, raising its vessel-severity macro-F_1 (0.686 [CI, 0.664 to 0.707]) above the untuned base model (0.513) and over twice the always-normal floor (0.312). CARDEA runs an end-to-end CAG pipeline from raw multi-view videos through keyframe selection to study-level diagnosis while exposing auditable spatial evidence behind its conclusions. RLVR on verifiable closed-ended tasks surfaced open-ended reporting ability that supervised imitation did not. Clinical use requires prospective validation against expert cardiologists.

title: Dynamic-Programming-Guided Hierarchical BPE and Empirical Analysis of Vocabulary Pruning
abstract: Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) constructs vocabularies through greedy pair merging, but the resulting merge order does not necessarily allocate a fixed model-visible vocabulary optimally for compression. We propose Dynamic-Programming-Guided Hierarchical BPE (DH-BPE), a vocabulary-construction method that combines token exposure under exact minimum-token segmentation with the hierarchical dependencies induced by BPE training. Starting from a modestly overshot BPE candidate vocabulary, DH-BPE uses dynamic programming to measure candidate utility and applies exposure-guided, dependency-aware pruning to select a fixed-size model-visible vocabulary. We compare DH-BPE against Standard BPE and recent vocabulary-optimization baselines, including Pruned BPE, MinGram, and MinGram-PP, in primary evaluations at 12K and 16K target vocabulary sizes, with an additional 18K evaluation against MinGram only. Across the primary 12K and 16K comparisons, DH-BPE consistently improves aggregate compression over Standard BPE, Pruned BPE, and MinGram under a shared exact minimum-token DP encoder. MinGram-PP achieves stronger aggregate compression in the primary comparisons, but DH-BPE outperforms it at overshoot factors f = 2.0 and f = 3.0 in cross-corpus evaluation; at 12K, MinGram-PP reverses this ordering only with the substantially larger candidate pools at f = 4.0 and f = 5.0. Qualitative analysis further shows that DH-BPE balances later, more complete BPE merges with reusable subword components, providing a practical approach to improving vocabulary allocation under a fixed model-visible vocabulary budget.

evidence.title: Dynamic-Programming-Guided Hierarchical BPE and Empirical Analysis of Vocabulary Pruning
evidence.abstract: Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) constructs vocabularies through greedy pair merging, but the resulting merge order does not necessarily allocate a fixed model-visible vocabulary optimally for compression. We propose Dynamic-Programming-Guided Hierarchical BPE (DH-BPE), a vocabulary-construction method that combines token exposure under exact minimum-token segmentation with the hierarchical dependencies induced by BPE training. Starting from a modestly overshot BPE candidate vocabulary, DH-BPE uses dynamic programming to measure candidate utility and applies exposure-guided, dependency-aware pruning to select a fixed-size model-visible vocabulary. We compare DH-BPE against Standard BPE and recent vocabulary-optimization baselines, including Pruned BPE, MinGram, and MinGram-PP, in primary evaluations at 12K and 16K target vocabulary sizes, with an additional 18K evaluation against MinGram only. Across the primary 12K and 16K comparisons, DH-BPE consistently improves aggregate compression over Standard BPE, Pruned BPE, and MinGram under a shared exact minimum-token DP encoder. MinGram-PP achieves stronger aggregate compression in the primary comparisons, but DH-BPE outperforms it at overshoot factors f = 2.0 and f = 3.0 in cross-corpus evaluation; at 12K, MinGram-PP reverses this ordering only with the substantially larger candidate pools at f = 4.0 and f = 5.0. Qualitative analysis further shows that DH-BPE balances later, more complete BPE merges with reusable subword components, providing a practical approach to improving vocabulary allocation under a fixed model-visible vocabulary budget.

title: AI-Driven Personalization and Consumer Decision-Making: How Perceived Value and Cognitive Bias Shape Consumer Responses
abstract: Objective: This study aims to analyze the influence of AI-driven personalization on Consumer Decision-Making through the mediating role of Perceived Value and to test the moderating role of Cognitive Bias in the relationships between AI-driven personalization and perceived value, as well as between Perceived Value and Consumer Decision-Making. Research Design & Methods: This study used a quantitative approach by surveying consumers who have experience interacting with AI-based digital platforms. The study population included all consumers who had experience using AI-based digital platforms in the past six months. The sample size was 240 respondents. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings: The results of the study indicate that AI-Driven Personalization does not directly influence Consumer Decision-Making. However, AI-Driven Personalization has been shown to have a positive effect on Perceived Value, and Perceived Value has a positive effect on Consumer Decision-Making. In addition, Perceived Value has been shown to significantly mediate the relationship between AI-Driven Personalization and Consumer Decision-Making. The results of the moderation test indicate that Cognitive Bias does not moderate the relationship between AI-Driven Personalization and Perceived Value, but strengthens the relationship between Perceived Value and Consumer Decision-Making. Contribution: This research provides a theoretical contribution by expanding the application of SOR Theory in the context of AI-based marketing by proving that the influence of AI-based personalization on consumer decisions occurs through the mechanism of forming perceived value. This research also enriches Behavioral Decision Theory by showing that psychological factors in the form of Cognitive Bias play a role in strengthening the transformation of value evaluations into actual consumer decisions. Novelty: The novelty of this research lies in the integration of AI-Driven Personalization, Perceived Value, and Cognitive Bias in a single conceptual model that combines the perspectives of SOR Theory and Behavioral Decision Theory. This research shows that the influence of AI-Driven Personalization on Consumer Decision-Making does not occur directly, but rather through Perceived Value as a mediator, while Cognitive Bias acts as a moderator that strengthens the relationship between Perceived Value and Consumer Decision-Making.

title: Neural Means and Kernel Corrections for Operator Learning
abstract: Kernel regression can fit prediction residuals or regress targets on learned features after neural training. We compare these two approaches on structural-mechanics and OCO-2 benchmarks, using ten random seeds for the main experiments. On structural mechanics, a corrected six-member stack reaches 4.546 ± 0.003% mean relative test error, close to PARA-Net's published 4.55%. With 1250 labels, the pipeline reaches 5.433 ± 0.093% against a published 6.49%. An analysis of sixty trained predictors shows limited scope for further improvement by global convex averaging within this pool: an empirical RMS lower bound of 4.814% is close to the hindsight optimum of 4.876%. On the O2 band, Matérn regression on raw inputs has approximately 40% relative error in the reduced coordinates, compared with 4.1% on frozen neural features. Coordinatewise selection gives lower ten-seed mean errors than the source emulator's stored predictions on all three bands under both criteria evaluated on the retained representation. Full-spectrum and retrieval accuracy are not evaluated. The analysis combines ensemble identities with conditional native-space error bounds. For uncertainty quantification, a constant-radius conformal set is narrower on average than a set scaled by the kernel power function.

title: Nota Técnica Breve sobre el Primer Piloto en Ecosistemas Tecnológicos de Producción
abstract: Este documento presenta una nota técnica breve sobre el primer piloto real de EcosistemIA aplicado a un ecosistema tecnológico de producción profesional durante 2026. El piloto se centró en validar la capacidad del modelo para mejorar la claridad operativa, reducir la carga cognitiva y estructurar documentación mínima viable en proyectos tecnológicos complejos. La intervención se realizó exclusivamente en la capa organizativa y documental, sin participar en decisiones técnicas ni revelar información sensible del proyecto. Los resultados preliminares muestran mejoras en la coherencia operativa, la velocidad de toma de decisiones y la sostenibilidad de los procesos internos. El caso se documenta de forma anónima siguiendo estándares de consultoría profesional y forma parte de la línea de investigación aplicada de EcosistemIA.

title: ##拓扑量子纠缠的自适应加密
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cryptographic algorithm, termed "拓扑量子纠缠的自适应加密"(TQC-AC), based on the principles of quantum entanglement and topological structures. The core innovation lies in the design of a dynamic topological structure that allows for adaptive key generation and secure data distribution in the presence of quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages the inherent properties of entangled particles to provide a fundamentally secure method of key management and data protection. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, explores its security properties, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its potential for robust cryptography. The focus is on demonstrating the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of existing cryptographic methods in the era of quantum computing.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry and Quantum Topology
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-Euclidean geometry to quantum topology, exploring the properties of quantum topology, developing computational methods based on quantum topology, and assessing their potential value in quantum information and quantum algorithms. We establish a quantum topology model based on non-Euclidean geometry, simulating quantum topology evolution, and leveraging quantum computation for this purpose. Traditional quantum topology research focuses on static properties of topology, aiming to explore the role of topology in dynamic processes, potentially leading to new quantum algorithms and information processing methods. This work seeks to advance our understanding of quantum topology and its implications for future technologies.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Feature Selection Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive feature selection algorithm designed to automatically optimize feature selection based on data distribution shifts. Traditional feature selection methods often lack the flexibility to adapt to evolving data patterns, leading to suboptimal model performance. This algorithm employs a dynamic adjustment mechanism to continuously re-evaluate and select the most relevant features, ensuring robustness and improved generalization. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that analyzes data distributions and iteratively refines feature selection decisions. The proposed algorithm offers a significant improvement over existing techniques, particularly in scenarios involving complex data dynamics, making it a valuable tool for machine learning practitioners.

title: Adaptive Machine Learning: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment Mechanism
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive machine learning model utilizing dynamic parameter adjustment to enhance model generalization and prediction accuracy. Traditional machine learning models often rely on fixed parameters, struggling to adapt to complex environmental changes. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts model parameters based on observed environmental shifts and inherent model characteristics, providing a more flexible and robust approach. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of experiments evaluating performance across diverse datasets. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop connecting environmental data, model performance, and parameter adjustments, enabling the model to continuously optimize itself. The presented work offers a significant advancement in adaptive learning, addressing limitations in traditional models and opening avenues for improved predictive capabilities.

title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Quantum Circuits for Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization through dynamically reconfigurable quantum circuits. The core concept involves adapting the structure of a quantum circuit during its execution, responding to real-time feedback derived from quantum state analysis. Traditional quantum circuit design often relies on static, pre-defined architectures, limiting their adaptability and potential for optimization. This work introduces a control system capable of monitoring qubit states and dynamically altering circuit topology – specifically, adjusting gate sequences and potentially even adding or removing qubits – to minimize gate count and maximize coherence, thereby improving overall algorithm efficiency. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the key components and operational principles of such a system, highlighting its potential to overcome the limitations of static circuits and usher in a new era of adaptive quantum computation. We demonstrate, through a mathematical model, how this dynamic reconfiguration can be strategically implemented to address specific algorithmic challenges, focusing on reducing circuit complexity and enhancing the fidelity of quantum computations. The key to this approach lies in continuous feedback loops and a sophisticated control algorithm that leverages quantum state information to guide circuit modifications. This allows for a more tailored and efficient execution of quantum algorithms compared to static designs.

title: Quantum Resonance Synchronization with Wave Function Collapse (QRWCC)
abstract: Quantum Resonance Synchronization with Wave Function Collapse (QRWCC) presents a novel approach to synchronizing quantum systems across multiple qubits, centered on a modified version of wave function collapse. This technique aims to enhance fidelity and coherence through a feedback loop driven by observed entanglement correlations. The core mechanism involves a quantum state evolution algorithm that dynamically adjusts the collapse of the wave function, mitigating the inherent noise associated with standard entanglement protocols. This approach represents a significant advancement in quantum synchronization, offering the potential for more robust and precise control over quantum states. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, analysis of its performance, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating improved fidelity and coherence compared to existing methods.
